content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Ink

The Mayor of London’s Gala

Danny Boyle brings a seismic moment in Rupert Murdoch’s Fleet Street career blazingly to life, employing the breathtaking style of a story torn from the headlines.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Danny Boyle

Screenwriter James Graham

With Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce, Claire Foy

UK 2026. 118min

Courtesy of STUDIOCANAL

Language English

Access information

Monday 12 October 21:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Tuesday 13 October 11:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 10:20

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In 1969, Rupert Murdoch acquired British tabloid The Sun, hiring gifted editor Larry Lamb to change the paper’s fortunes. Out of this devil’s pact, British journalism and society was forever changed. Boyle’s kinetic cinematic energy is matched by Guy Pearce and Jack O’Connell’s muscular performances as the men who exploded Fleet Street, British mores and political fortunes.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use, graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

Contains sexist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Screen Talk: Danny Boyle

The director of Ink joins us for this Screen Talk, to discuss a career that has placed him among the most successful British filmmakers.

All About the Money

The heir of one of America’s wealthiest families, who has ambitions to rebel against values he now despises, is the subject of Sinéad O’Shea’s compelling documentary portrait.

Tender Loving Care

In a world that feels increasingly untethered from human connection, the incomparable Mike Leigh returns with a thought-provoking and compassionate view of urban life.

content.article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

Lady

In a bustling Lagos, a solitary female taxi driver finds community among a group of sex workers as she transports them around the city.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Olive Nwosu

With Jessica Gabriel’s Ujah, Amanda Oruh, Tinuade Jemiseye

UK-Nigeria 2026. 93min

Courtesy of Metis Films

Language Nigerian Pidgin With English subtitles

Access information

Saturday 10 October 21:00

Audio description

Tuesday 13 October 12:10

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Lady works long and lonely hours, saving up money with hopes of escaping to Freetown, in Sierra Leone. When childhood friend and sex worker Pinky asks for her help, Lady agrees but soon finds her life upended. The fantastic, mainly female cast shared the Sundance Film Festival Special Jury Award for Acting Ensemble. It’s easy to see why, with this character-driven film that is also a stunning portrait of a vibrant, sleepless city.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Clarissa

Sophie Okonedo shines in Arie and Chuko Esiri’s (Eyimofe, LFF 2020) sophomore feature film, a delicate, sun-soaked re-imagining of Mrs Dalloway, set in contemporary Lagos.

Filipiñana

This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.

Our Share of Sand

Shalini Adnani’s poignant coming-of-age drama presents a unique perspective on India’s gaping class inequality, child labour and the deep corruption underpinning a family’s economic status.

content.article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

Forest High

Forêt Ivre

In this visually arresting film, solo caretakers keep the fires burning in a remote Alpine chalet where weary hikers find modest lodgings.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Manon Coubia

With Salomé Richard, Aurélia Petit, Anne Coesens

Belgium-France 2026. 103min

Courtesy of Rai Cinema International Distribution

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Anne, Hélène and Suzanne each take a season as hut master. As the landscape morphs throughout the year, a vivid portrait of these women emerges; each resolute in their independence and comfort in this self-imposed solitude. With its gentle observations of natural and human interactions, Manon Coubia’s award-winning debut is a sublime offering for harried urban dwellers.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

9 Temples to Heaven

Infused with gentle humour and profound humanity, Sompot Chidgasornpongse’s fiction debut presents a serene passage through family, faith and the cycles of life.

Concrete Turned to Sand

Shaped by the tidal rhythms of British Columbia’s oyster farms, this richly cinematic documentary, shot on 35mm, exists where labour, scientific inquiry and the living world meet.

My Wife Cries

German filmmaker Angela’s Schanelec continues to mine the vagaries of the human psyche with this masterful study of a relationship in freefall.

Films and events

Galas

Being Heumann

British actor Ruth Madeley is outstanding as Judith Heumann, the activist who helped fight for anti-discrimination laws for individuals with disabilities, in CODA director Siân Heder’s enthralling film.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Siân Heder

Screenwriters Siân Heder, Rebekah Taussig

With Ruth Madeley, Madeline Delp, Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Rob Delaney

USA 2026. 127min

Courtesy of Apple TV

Language English

Access information

Monday 12 October 17:45

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Tuesday 13 October 14:15

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Friday 16 October 14:50

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Featuring an exceptional ensemble, including Mark Ruffalo and Dylan O’Brien, Heder’s precisely rendered drama recreates the battle between government officials and the activists, culminating in their 28-day takeover of San Francisco’s Federal Building in 1977. What emerges is a vision of a tenacious, witty collective of history-makers whose groundbreaking act of resistance was instrumental in bringing much-needed social change.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of ableism and drug use.

Contains ableist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Slightest Touch

The power of friendship and connection is explored in Rachel Fleit’s soulful and life-affirming documentary, featuring Emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell.

Rebellion

Revolution is the beat that drums through this electrifying story about the landmark case against the Bradford 12.

Adam Pearson: Zero Intention of Living Quietly

Actor, broadcaster, and leading disability advocate Adam Pearson joins us to discuss his career and his influential advocacy work for more inclusive storytelling and authentic representation.

Films and events

Documentary Competition

Concrete Turned to Sand

Shaped by the tidal rhythms of British Columbia’s oyster farms, this richly cinematic documentary, shot on 35mm, exists where labour, scientific inquiry and the living world meet.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriters Jessica Johnson, Ryan Ermacora

Canada 2026. 73min

Courtesy of Slag Pile Films Ltd

Language English

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 14:15

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Shimmering underwater images of shellfish suspended in shifting currents and spectral nocturnal scenes lend this film an almost otherworldly beauty, as though moments from science fiction had surfaced within everyday life. With a contemplative rhythm and patient gaze, Jessica Johnson and Ryan Ermacora expand our perception of space and time, gently unsettling familiar ways of seeing and revealing the hidden transformations of the landscape.

Hyun Jin Cho

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

To Hold a Mountain

Set in the remote highlands of Montenegro, this year’s Sundance World Documentary Prize winner reflects on the fragile coexistence between ancestral knowledge and the growing pressures of the contemporary world.

Forest High

In this visually arresting film, solo caretakers keep the fires burning in a remote Alpine chalet where weary hikers find modest lodgings.

Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff

This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.

Films and events

Official Competition

Imperium

Master of archival film reconstruction, Sergei Loznitsa, reframes Soviet history once again via the revealing gaze of Italian cameramen who captured life there in the early 1970s.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Sergei Loznitsa

Germany-France-Italy-Lithuania 2026. 176min

Courtesy of Coproduction Office

Introduction

The footage Loznitsa uncovered at Rome’s Audiovisual Archive of the Labour and Democratic Movement left him marvelling at the contrast with official Soviet productions from the same era. Opening in Moscow, the film shifts into territories where different traits, beliefs and ethnographic features emerge, revealing the powerful grip of an empire over its people. The result is a compelling indictment of Russia’s historical and present-day imperialism.

Sergio Fant

With thanks to German Films.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

Our programmers recommend...

Minotaur

Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme infidèle to contemporary Russia, delivering a magnificent political allegory that dissects the mechanics of ego, violence and corruption.

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.

Films and events

Journey

Clarissa

Sophie Okonedo shines in Arie and Chuko Esiri’s (Eyimofe, LFF 2020) sophomore feature film, a delicate, sun-soaked re-imagining of Mrs Dalloway, set in contemporary Lagos.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors Arie Esiri, Chuko Esiri

Screenwriter Chuko Esiri

With Sophie Okonedo, David Oyelowo, India Amarteifio

Nigeria-USA 2026. 134min

Courtesy of NEON

Languages English, Nigerian Pidgin With some English subtitles

Introduction

It’s the day of Clarissa’s garden party. Just as she’s set to reunite with old friends, she finds herself reflecting on a summer that shaped the course of their lives. Virginia Woolf’s beloved novel is the jumping-off point for this rich and captivating look at class and gender in contemporary Nigerian society.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and self-harm.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Dao

The new film by Alain Gomis is a formally inventive, politically attuned meditation on the enduring ties of the African diaspora, and the meaning of family and community.

The Last Day

Acclaimed visual artist Rachel Rose gives Mrs Dalloway a contemporary makeover in her arresting mood piece, starring Alicia Vikander and Victoria Pedretti.

Mouse

Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy.

content.article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

Ben’Imana

This Cannes Camera d’Or winner unfolds in the shadow of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, exploring its legacy and the possibility of forgiveness.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo

Screenwriters Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, Delphine Agut

With Clémentine U. Nyirinkindi, Isabelle Kabano, Kesia Kelly Nishimwe

Rwanda-France-Gabon-Norway 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Alexander

Language Kinyarwanda With English subtitles

Introduction

A survivor of the Rwandan genocide tries to lead her community toward reconciliation and to foster dialogue between victims and the families of perpetrators. Generations of women share different perspectives as they confront their trauma together, in an intimate and thoughtful film about resilience, sisterhood and communal healing.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of sexual violence.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lady

In a bustling Lagos, a solitary female taxi driver finds community among a group of sex workers as she transports them around the city.

Variations on a Theme

The Tiger Award winner at this year’s Rotterdam Film Festival is a gentle and enchanting portrait of an octogenarian goat herder in South Africa’s Kamiesberge.

House of the Wind

Cameroonian director Bernard Auguste Kouemo Yanghu’s outstanding feature debut is a poignant tale of an ageing parent who has been left behind.

Films and events

Dare

Life of Jorge Luis Borges

Mariano Llinás’ epic contemplation of the life and works of Jorge Luis Borges is every bit as wily and playful as the Argentine writer’s stories.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Mariano Llinás

With Ernesto Montequín, Mariano Llinás, Laura Paredes

Argentina 2026. 343min (includes two 10-minute intervals after Part 1 and Part 2, respectively)

Courtesy of Luxbox

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

This layered portrait of one of Argentina’s and, Llinás argues, the 20th century’s most important writers, is constructed through assembled objects, with a strong focus on place. It’s also as much a film about the process of making a film that refuses any categorisation. Witty, insightful and enigmatic, it’s quite unlike anything you might see this year.

Maria Delgado

Features a discussion of racism and domestic abuse.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Making Marie Antoinette

Eleanor Coppola’s documentary on the making of Marie Antoinette is a rousing love letter to filmic craft and the joys and complexities of leading an artistic life.

Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.

Glaxo

An act of betrayal between a close group of friends has terrible consequences in Benjamín Naishtat’s atmospheric period noir.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

At Night

Beatrice Gibson’s feature directorial debut is a luminous nocturne, evocatively capturing the streets of Paris over the course of a single night on 16mm.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Beatrice Gibson

With Diocouda Diaoune, Kátia Belo Cardoso, Sophie Robinson

UK-France 2026. 87min

Courtesy of Somesuch

Languages English, French, Bambara, Mandarin Chinese With some English subtitles

Introduction

Inspired by the poetry of Alice Notley and other avant-garde literary figures, At Night moves with Gibson and a group of women in their forties as they share intimate reflections on desire, creativity, motherhood, sexuality and identity. Blending chance encounters, lived experiences and imagined worlds, it unfolds as a poetic, oneiric tapestry of voices, memories and possibilities, carried along by a hypnotic synth score.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Chronovisor

The film collective Cosmic Salon (Jack Auen and Kevin Walker) make their beguiling and assured feature debut, guiding us through hidden histories and uncanny landscapes of belief, mystery and the unknown.

Tropical Fractals

Leonardo Pirondi’s timely reflection on ecological collapse imagines a future in which a biodome spaceship preserves the last traces of life on Earth.

The Last Day

Acclaimed visual artist Rachel Rose gives Mrs Dalloway a contemporary makeover in her arresting mood piece, starring Alicia Vikander and Victoria Pedretti.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Shorts

Altered States

Fractured memories and uncertain fates are examined in shorts featuring our unshakeable resolve.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Total running time 109min

Programmed by Sky Lewis, Victoria Millington

Content advice This short film programme contains flashing images, racist attitudes and language, scenes of harm towards children, and themes of drug use and domestic violence or abuse.

Mon Taxi

Watch for free on BFI Player until 25 October

Director-screenwriter Meriem Sakrouhi

Morocco-USA 2026. 8min

Meriem, who for years called her father every day, decides to call him on the day after his death.

Bundle

Director-screenwriter Carlo Milillo

UK 2026. 13min

In this tale of grief and loss, something isn’t right when Will heads to a party to meet his brother.

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

To the North

Director-screenwriter Amer Nasser

Palestine 2026. 8min

In 2025, after a brief ceasefire in Gaza, Firas returns alone to the north to search for his sister and her family.

Content advice

Contains scenes of harm towards children.

(Failing to Make) A Documentary About My Sudanese Family

Director Sid Elbadawi

UK-Sudan 2026. 15min

Setting out to document a family holiday in the shadow of a civil war, a filmmaker finds the process unravelling the film itself.

Content advice

Contains themes of drug use.

Contains racist attitudes and language.

Stolen Memories

Stjålne Minner

Director-screenwriter Anders Davidsen

Norway-Sweden 2026. 18min

Eighteen-year-old Emil’s night turns to horror when his girlfriend discovers some childhood photos, forcing him to question his past.

Content advice

Contains themes of domestic violence or abuse.

Forgotten Spaceman

Director Elham Ehsas

UK-Afghanistan 2026. 16min

In 1988, Afghanistan sent its first and only astronaut, Abdul Ahad Momand, into space, creating a fleeting moment of hope.

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

White Musk

Watch for free on BFI Player until 25 October

Director-screenwriter Fatima Wardy

Sudan-USA 2026. 18min

Tensions arise when a young Sudanese woman becomes her mother’s primary caregiver.

FarEye

Watch for free on BFI Player until 25 October

Director-screenwriter Hayden Mclean

UK 2026. 13min

Fleeing the chaos of home, a young Jamaican boy finds refuge within a community guided by music, spirit and faith.

Content advice

Contains scenes of domestic violence or abuse.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

As the Years Roll By

In reflecting on the past or embracing unexpected futures, time flows through people’s connection with others and the earth, in these shorts on life in the later years.

I See Myself

From silent protests and secret ponderings to vocal uprisings and drastic acts, watch people endeavour to carve a bigger space for themselves in a world that’s trying to box them in.

Call Your Bluff

Whether it’s cutting your own hair, winning the lottery, looking for love or livening up a dull day at work, these uk shorts will cover all your comedy needs.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

Lemonade

Barry Keoghan plays a social worker trying to make up for the past in this heartfelt coming-of-age Irish drama about second chances.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Kim Bartley

With Lewis Brophy, Carla Tous, Barry Keoghan

Ireland-UK 2026. 112min

Courtesy of MetFilm Distribution

Language English

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 13:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Having turned 18, Danny (bright newcomer Lewis Brophy) has to leave the foster care system to find a job and stay out of trouble. He reconnects with Josh, his former care worker in need of redemption, and a mysterious girl who might help turn his life around. Kim Bartley’s narrative debut is an intimate and delicate drama that shines a light on the power of love, friendship and human connections.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

7 Miles Out

Carol Morley (Dreams of a Life, The Falling) adapts her moving semi-autobiographical novel, capturing her adolescence in Stockport during the 70s and 80s.

A Place to Heal

Cédric Kahn’s watchful drama deftly captures life within an adolescent psychiatric unit, from the carers’ work to the kids’ trauma, friendships and lust for life.

Tender Loving Care

In a world that feels increasingly untethered from human connection, the incomparable Mike Leigh returns with a thought-provoking and compassionate view of urban life.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Rose

Sandra Hüller gives an award-winning performance as a 17th-century female soldier who disguises herself as a man to gain acceptance in a brutal farming community.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Markus Schleinzer

Screenwriters Markus Schleinzer, Alexander Brom

With Sandra Hüller, Caro Braun, Marisa Growaldt

Austria-Germany 2026. 94min

Courtesy of MUBI

Language German With English subtitles

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 18:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Thursday 15 October 15:10

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In the aftermath of the ferocious Thirty Years’ War, a scarred female soldier dangerously inveigles her way into a strict rural community by posing as a man with an inheritance. Seemingly dispassionate in its watchful, austere monochrome, yet quietly devastating in its unflinching look at gender-based prejudice and intolerance, Markus Schleinzer’s masterful film is another triumph for Hüller.

Leigh Singer

With thanks to the Austrian Cultural Forum London.

Content advice

Contains scenes of sexual violence.

Contains transphobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Fatherland

In a masterclass of control and precision, Paweł Pawlikowski explores the fragmented soul of postwar Germany through a father-daughter road trip dominated by personal ghosts.

Woman Unknown

In May el-Toukhy’s powerful third feature, Marie, a survivor with secrets, navigates retribution and the febrile chaos of life in post-war Denmark.

Everytime

Sandra Wollner’s film, winner of Un Certain Regard at Cannes this year, is an enigmatic exploration of grief and the path to healing.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Behemoth!

BFI Patrons’ Gala

Michael Clayton director Tony Gilroy returns with a stylishly crafted portrait of a beguiling classical musician, played by Pedro Pascal.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Tony Gilroy

With Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett

USA 2026. 127min

Courtesy of Searchlight Pictures

Language English

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 18:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Wednesday 14 October 11:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Friday 16 October 15:20

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Cello prodigy Alex has spent his adult life changing orchestra chairs and lovers’ beds at regular intervals. On the run from his latest fling, he retreats to LA as a session player and into the suspended reality of a film score studio. Gilroy’s inventive script is rich in narrative textures, shape-shifting across time to explore the mysteries and complexities of the human heart. He’s ably supported by Pascal and a superb cast that includes Olivia Wilde and Will Arnett.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Congo Boy

Set in the Central African Republic, Rafiki Fariala’s melodic autobiographical feature follows a young refugee who, against all odds, chases his musical dreams.

The Man I Love

Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.

The Liberation

In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.

Films and events

Laugh

The History of Concrete

Having attended a Hallmark movie workshop, John Wilson applies his learnings to a documentary about concrete, albeit with a dryly funny and deceptively understated tone.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director John Wilson

USA 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Visit Films

Language English

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 18:15

Descriptive subtitles

Wednesday 14 October 20:35

Relaxed screening – buy tickets for this screening

Descriptive subtitles

Thursday 15 October 20:45

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 15:45

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

After finding himself with too much time on his hands, documentarian Wilson attends a workshop on how to make Hallmark romcoms. It inspires him to apply the formula to a film investigating the story of concrete. Infused with Wilson’s trademark curiosity and wit, the film project introduces him to a variety of unusual people and places. The result is a wry and humane meditation on the modern world.

Chloé Trayner

Content advice

Contains ableist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Wicker

Olivia Colman gives yet another bravura performance in this delightfully offbeat comedy, playing an outcast from her village who orders herself a wicker husband.

The Banning Curse

Iranian director Mohsen Amiryousefi discusses his eventful career with the Angel of Death in this hilarious cinematic autofiction about the highs and lows of radical filmmaking.

It Gets Worse

Leo Reich’s new series turns the struggles of young Londoners into its playground, mining a generation’s problems for biting, clever comedy.

Films and events

Love

Flies

Moscas

Fernando Eimbcke’s fifth feature, a gentle black-and-white comedy set in a gloriously retro-feel Mexico City, sees an unlikely friendship emerge between a cantankerous landlady and her unexpected tenant.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Fernando Eimbcke

Screenwriters Vanesa Garnica, Fernando Eimbcke

With Teresa Sánchez, Bastian Escobar, Hugo Ramírez

Mexico 2026. 99min

Courtesy of Alpha Violet

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

Olga is not having the best of times. To obtain some extra cash, she decides to rent a room to Tulio, one of the relatives of a cancer patient at the nearby hospital, unaware of the fact that that he is also sneaking his young son into the accommodation. Eimbcke’s wonderful film is a witty companion piece to Duck Season, his engaging feature debut.

Maria Delgado

With thanks to Embassy of Mexico in the United Kingdom.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

La Perra

Acclaimed Chilean director Dominga Sotomayor delivers a beautifully shot character-driven study of dependency, loneliness and the complex relationship between past and present.

The Meltdown

Sutherland Award winner Manuela Martelli delivers a knife-edge thriller centring on the disappearance of a teenager in a remote Chilean resort.

Isabel

Gabe Klinger’s film, shot on 16mm, is a gentle, warm and beautifully observed love letter to the pleasures of wine.

Films and events

Documentary Competition

Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing

Erik Shirai’s beautifully shot and fascinating film grants rare access inside the disciplined inner domain of Japan’s sumo wrestling world.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Erik Shirai

Japan-USA-UK-Denmark 2026. 99min

Courtesy of ESPN Films

Languages Japanese, Mongolian With English subtitles

Introduction

In pop culture, sumo wrestling isn’t always treated with the seriousness it deserves. But in this gripping film, Shirai repositions it as an ancient sport whose competitors are forced to submit to gruelling training. Unfolding over the course of a year, Sumo follows a number of fighters, highlighting their dedication and the sacrifices they make in order to be the very best.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.

The Match

Few sporting contests loom as large in the public imagination as the dramatic 1986 World Cup Quarter Final between England and Argentina, as this documentary details.

Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson share a dream of becoming the first to successfully climb up and ski down the north face of Everest – a feat that prompts concern among friends and family. The resulting film is a compelling and moving portrait of perseverance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Films and events

Create

The Friend’s House is Here

Khaneh Doost Injast

A dancer and a playwright juggle the mundanities of living together with the struggles of creative practice as part of Iran’s underground art scene.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriters Hossein Keshavarz, Maryam Ataei

With Mahshad Bahraminejad, Hana Mana, Farzad Namavari

Iran-USA 2026. 95min

Courtesy of Alma Linda Film

Language Persian With English subtitles

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 18:30

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Hanna and Pari have found ways to make political art under the radar, avoiding Iran’s strict censorship through secret plays and long, food-fuelled hangouts in their flat. But when Pari puts on her latest play, she and Hanna must face the realities of their situation. Shot in secret and smuggled into the Sundance Film Festival, this is a hangout movie with an urgent political charge.

Grace Barber-Plentie

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Concrete Land

Asmahan Bkerat’s feature directorial debut is an intimate, multi-generational portrait of a mixed-raced family fighting displacement and hostility in Jordan.

Revolutionaries Never Die

Framed as a cinematic letter to the late Lebanese filmmaker Jocelyne Saab, this evocative and timely work reanimates Saab’s 16mm archive as a living space of dialogue and political imagination.

Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.

Films and events

Thrill

The Meltdown

El Deshielo

Sutherland Award winner Manuela Martelli delivers a knife-edge thriller centring on the disappearance of a teenager in a remote Chilean resort.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Manuela Martelli

With Maya O’Rourke, Saskia Rosendahl, Maia Rae Domagala

Chile-USA-Spain-Mexico 2026. 118min

Courtesy of Les Films du Losange

Languages Spanish, English, German With English subtitles

Introduction

It is 1992 and while watching the comings and goings in her family’s hotel, nine-year-old Inés befriends Hanna, one of the German skiers training in the area. When Hanna goes missing, Inés observes the local community closing ranks without quite understanding what is happening. Focussing on what lies unsaid, Martelli (1976, LFF 2022) expertly captures the tensions of a society as it transitions to democracy.

Maria Delgado

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

My Notes on Mars

In Lili Horvát’s beguiling third feature, the sudden return of Sam’s missing wife, who has no memory of anything except her scientific research, gives their relationship another chance.

Glaxo

An act of betrayal between a close group of friends has terrible consequences in Benjamín Naishtat’s atmospheric period noir.

Flies

Fernando Eimbcke’s fifth feature, a gentle black-and-white comedy set in a gloriously retro-feel Mexico City, sees an unlikely friendship emerge between a cantankerous landlady and her unexpected tenant.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Thrill

Josephine

Winner of the Grand Jury Dramatic Prize at Sundance, this suspenseful and devastating film follows a child trying to navigate life after witnessing a sexual assault.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Beth de Araújo

With Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan

USA 2026. 119min

Courtesy of Curzon

Language English

Certificate BBFC18

Introduction

Eight-year-old Josephine (an astounding performance by newcomer Mason Reeves) knows that she saw something bad, but struggles to find answers. Her parents (a brilliant Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) grapple with how to comfort her. Weaving thriller and horror conventions within a serious and sobering scenario, Beth de Araújo creates an often uncomfortable yet vital film that interrogates how we explain the unspeakable.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, sex, and sexual violence.

Contains flashing images.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Girl Unknown

Jing Zou’s captivating debut feature, an intimate, decade-spanning character study, explores the consequences of the single-child policy on generations of Chinese girls.

Prima Facie

Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo gives a captivating central performance in Susanna White’s much-anticipated screen adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play.

The Liberation

In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Sean Mathias

Screenwriter Martin Sherman

With Ian McKellen, Roger Allam, Joanna Lumley

UK 2026. 109min

Courtesy of Icon Film Distribution

Language English

Introduction

Meet Frank and Percy, an unlikely pair, who strike up a friendship while dog walking on Hampstead Heath. Soon enough, their platonic bond quietly blossoms into something far more tender. Featuring a star-studded ensemble including Stephen Fry, Joanna Lumley, Derek Jacobi, Ncuti Gatwa and Siân Phillips, this charming tale of late-blooming love is a warm-hearted and soul-searching gem.

Wema Mumma

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Elsinore

Andrew Scott is a towering presence in this singular account of Ian Charleson’s life, capturing the moment when he faced his own mortality as he prepared to play Hamlet at the Royal National Theatre.

The Idiot(s)

Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film.

Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!

Recently widowed Haru rediscovers her love for ballroom dancing, only to find herself attracted to her new instructor, in this zany, toe-tapping film.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

French Girls

Effortlessly moving from one moment to the next, Hyun Lee’s fashionably hip and charming micro-budget debut heralds an exciting directorial talent.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Hyun Lee

With Mia Kidis, Daia, Anya Beyersdorf

Australia 2026. 83min

Courtesy of Preliminary Materials Films Pty Ltd

Language English

Introduction

Mia is happily aimless, working odd jobs and hanging with friends. But when she’s scouted to become a model, new people and strange conundrums enter the frame. Showcasing an array of new talent, both in front of and behind the camera, Lee’s inventive exploration of the absurdity of 20-something life, unfolding against the backdrop of late-stage capitalism, is a welcome and unexpected breath of fresh cinematic air.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Atlantic Rhapsody

A young man embarks on a surreal quest to find his long-lost father in a remarkable feature debut that spans 20 years of recent Chinese history.

Filipiñana

This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.

The Fox

A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Documentary Competition

Queer Edward II

This all-archival tour de force takes us behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s Edward II, set against the backdrop of the anti-LGBTQIA+ legislation of 1980s Britain.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Theo Rollason

UK 2026. 97min

Courtesy of Lightborn Films

Language English

Access information

Sunday 11 October 18:00

Audio description

Tuesday 13 October 20:45

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 19:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

This all-archival tour de force takes us behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s Edward II, set against the backdrop of the anti-LGBTQIA+ legislation of 1980s Britain. In 1991, Jarman started production on Edward II, just as queer life in the UK was under renewed threat from the British government. Seamus McGarvey captured all the drama on set in a previously unseen treasure trove of behind-the-scenes footage. Queer Edward II masterfully reanimates this archive as a vigorous and radical reflection on the power of art as protest.

Chloé Trayner

Content advice

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Act 3

The latest in Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor’s series of cinematic essays is a rich and thought-provoking journey through ageing, legacy and the intersection between artistic and personal relationships.

Elsinore

Andrew Scott is a towering presence in this singular account of Ian Charleson’s life, capturing the moment when he faced his own mortality as he prepared to play Hamlet at the Royal National Theatre.

The Man I Love: Remembering the AIDS Crisis

This event gives space for remembrance and reflection on the legacy and lasting impact of the AIDS epidemic.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

Ana, en passant

Fernanda Salgado’s gorgeous animation is a travelogue of memories, ancestral connections and the future experiences that shape one’s identity.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Fernanda Salgado

With Jéssica Pierina, Zezé Motta, Carlos Francisco

Brazil-Portugal-France 2026. 90min

Courtesy of Miyu Distribution

Languages Portuguese, French With English subtitles

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 20:50

Descriptive subtitles

Wednesday 14 October 16:15

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Feeling lost after her beloved grandmother dies, Ana travels from Brazil to Paris to follow in her relative’s footsteps. It’s a journey that allows her to discover more about her family, heritage and, ultimately, herself. Salgado brings her animation radiantly to life, infusing real-life footage that gives greater depth to the bustling surroundings – the vibrant cities to which this textured film is a paean.

Isabel Moir

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Marie Madeleine

The second feature from Haitian actor-director Gessica Généus (Freda, LFF 2021) follows an unlikely friendship between a sex worker and preacher’s son that rocks their community.

9 Temples to Heaven

Infused with gentle humour and profound humanity, Sompot Chidgasornpongse’s fiction debut presents a serene passage through family, faith and the cycles of life.

Ba’s Book

Ashley Duong crafts a heartfelt hybrid film in response to her father’s memoir, which recounts his experiences of the Vietnam War and Iranian Revolution.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Chronicles from the Siege

Winner of the Best First Feature Award at the Berlin International Film Festival this year, Abdallah Al-Khatib’s fiction debut traces the daily lives of Palestinian citizens trapped in a war zone.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Abdallah Al-Khatib

With Nadim Rimawi, Saja Kilani, Ahmed Zitouni

Algeria-France-Palestine 2026. 98min

Courtesy of Loco Films

Language Arabic With English subtitles

Introduction

In this bold and defiant film, divided into five interconnected stories, the occupants of a military-occupied war zone find the foundational things in life – food, sex, safely giving birth – become matters of life and death as they scrabble for survival. Al-Kahtib’s film is an articulate reminder of the importance of connection, even in the darkest of times.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Mariinka

Shot over ten years, this unflinching portrait of youth in Eastern Ukraine is a rare and powerful account of the passing of time during conflict.

Concrete Land

Asmahan Bkerat’s feature directorial debut is an intimate, multi-generational portrait of a mixed-raced family fighting displacement and hostility in Jordan.

Az Zeeb

Discovering a cache of Super 8 home movies and photographs following the death of his grandmother, Chilean filmmaker Rafael Guendelman embarks on a personal journey through his family’s intertwined political histories.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

Tutu

Sam Pollard’s impressively researched and rich archival documentary is an incisive portrait of one of the most beloved public figures of the 20th century.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Sam Pollard

UK-South Africa 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Hidden Light

Languages English, Afrikaans With some English subtitles

Introduction

For a man who possessed an impish, joyful persona, Archbishop Desmond Tutu brought nerves of steel and a fierce intelligence to his fight against Apartheid in South Africa and beating a path to national reconciliation. Pollard’s engaging film gives primacy to Tutu’s political life, but smartly orientates this within a fulsome portrait of a man whose unshakeable belief in humanity continues to inspire long after his passing.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, racism, and racist violence.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

14th

Ten years after her Emmy Award-winning 13th, Ava DuVernay returns to the US Constitution with a probing look at the thorny history of the 14th amendment.

The Story of Documentary Film (The 1990s)

This fascinating chapter from Mark Cousins’ epic essay on the history of documentary chronicles a decade of formal reinvention and mainstream success.

Dao

The new film by Alain Gomis is a formally inventive, politically attuned meditation on the enduring ties of the African diaspora, and the meaning of family and community.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Prima Facie

Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo gives a captivating central performance in Susanna White’s much-anticipated screen adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Susanna White

Screenwriter Suzie Miller

With Cynthia Erivo, Daniel Ings, Toheeb Jimoh, Noma Dumezweni, Elliot Levey

UK-Australia 2026. 106min

Courtesy of Sony Pictures Releasing UK

Language English

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 21:15

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Friday 16 October 20:50

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 11:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Tessa is an ambitious barrister, used to winning and dominating in the courtroom by defending men accused of sexual assault. But when she unexpectedly becomes the accuser in a sexual assault case, she is forced to confront the legal system that she once trusted. This is a powerful exploration of a woman’s fight for justice and the power dynamics at play in a patriarchal world.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex and sexual violence.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Screen Talk: Cynthia Erivo

As she prepares to unveil her mesmerising performance in Prima Facie, we welcome Cynthia Erivo to this Screen Talk.

The Debut

For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore.

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

The second part of Julia Loktev’s epic documentary, detailing the persecution of journalists in Russia, follows her brave protagonists’ escape abroad following the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Julia Loktev

USA 2026. 370min (includes 15min interval)

Courtesy of Cinetic

Language Russian With English subtitles

Introduction

Part one of this extraordinary undertaking chronicled the work of young female journalists who faced growing repression by Vladimir Putin’s regime in the lead-up to the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. This new instalment proves even more troubling, finding the journalists scattered across different countries and grappling with their new lives, while still struggling to continue their reporting on Russia.

Sergio Fant

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Mariinka

Shot over ten years, this unflinching portrait of youth in Eastern Ukraine is a rare and powerful account of the passing of time during conflict.

The Whisper of Sunlight

Acclaimed documentarian Wong Siu-pong’s moving film creates an intimate space in which three young women with terminal conditions navigate experiences of illness, care and companionship.

Imperium

Master of archival film reconstruction, Sergei Loznitsa, reframes Soviet history once again via the revealing gaze of Italian cameramen who captured life there in the early 1970s.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Create

Zero Intention of Living Quietly

This uplifting portrait chronicles Adam Pearson’s journey to transform his love of movies into a career on screen while living with neurofibromatosis.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Edward Lovelace

UK 2026. 87min

Courtesy of Ventureland

Language English With English subtitles

Access information

Sunday 11 October 15:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Wednesday 14 October 12:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Pearson grew up watching movies but never saw his disability reflected on screen. When he is offered his first acting role, he is uncertain about the spotlight it will inevitably generate, but an unlikely friendship with a young girl who also has NF1 gives Adam the inspiration to take centre stage, in this life-affirming story of embracing difference and chasing our dreams.

Chloé Trayner

Content advice

Contains scenes of ableism.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Slightest Touch

The power of friendship and connection is explored in Rachel Fleit’s soulful and life-affirming documentary, featuring Emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell.

Being Heumann

British actor Ruth Madeley is outstanding as Judith Heumann, the activist who helped fight for anti-discrimination laws for individuals with disabilities, in CODA director Siân Heder’s enthralling film.

Adam Pearson: Zero Intention of Living Quietly

Actor, broadcaster, and leading disability advocate Adam Pearson joins us to discuss his career and his influential advocacy work for more inclusive storytelling and authentic representation.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Family

Julián

Cartoon Saloon’s heartfelt animated tale about a boy who is proud to be different is a surefire hit.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Louise Bagnall

Screenwriter juliany taveras

With Knyght Darius Jack, Milcania Diaz-Rojas

Ireland-Luxembourg-Canada-Denmark 2026. 85min

Courtesy of Cartoon Saloon

Language English

Introduction

Young Julián, a bright child with a love of bling and sparkles, is sent to Brooklyn to stay with his Dominican grandmother. It’s tough initially, but when he learns about the forthcoming Mermaid Parade, something clicks – he is a mermaid! This flawless and uplifting film from LFF favourites Cartoon Saloon is a celebration of what it means to be young, different and loved.

Justin Johnson

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Iron Boy

With its smooth, hand-painted style, Iron Boy is a warm, moving animation about an 11-year-old boy who is forced to rethink his outlook on the world when he receives a life-changing diagnosis.

My Friend the Sun

In this engrossing and brightly coloured animated triumph, a young girl is transported to the home of the Mexican gods and has to fight to find her way back home.

The Mermaid Parade

This magical crafting adventure is inspired by the captivating film Julián.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Possible Love

Ga-neung-han sa-rang

Lee Chang-dong’s masterfully directed follow-up to Burning (LFF 2018) finds four strangers’ lives entwined by hidden desires and repressed emotions.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Lee Chang-dong

Screenwriters Lee Chang-dong, Oh Jung-mi

With Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung, Cho Yeo-jeong

South Korea 2026. 164min

Courtesy of Netflix

Language Korean With English subtitles

Introduction

A chance meeting introduces filmmaker Ye-ji to Mi-ok’s family, whose lives have been affected by her husband’s unemployment. They’re perfect subjects for her documentary on workers who have been made redundant, leading them to spend more time in Ye-ji and her husband’s world. But as their connection deepens, the stark contrast between their class and background sees fractures appear in the collaboration, forcing them to confront their marriages and the wider world they all inhabit.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

All of a Sudden

Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s delivers an audiaciously tender, transcendent study of humanity through the subtle account of a life-changing encounter.

Hearing

Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

Films and events

Laugh

Wicker

Olivia Colman gives yet another bravura performance in this delightfully offbeat comedy, playing an outcast from her village who orders herself a wicker husband.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors-screenwriters Alex Huston Fischer, Eleanor Wilson

With Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Elizabeth Debicki

USA 2026. 105min

Courtesy of Black Bear

Language English

Access information

Thursday 8 October 17:45

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Saturday 10 October 12:00

Audio description

Wednesday 14 October 15:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Fisherwoman is unmarried, allegedly smelly, constantly teased by her small-minded neighbours and desperate to keep to herself. But when she decides to see what life would be like with a very particular kind of mail-order husband, what arrives (a statuesque Alexander Skarsgård) soon sparks jealousy and creates chaos. Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson’s wonderfully eccentric fable is, at its core, a gentle love story.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Idiot(s)

Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film.

Wild Horse Nine

Martin McDonagh continues to mine the absurdities and complexities of male relationships in a film that brims with energy and is sure to delight.

The Debut

For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore.
