content.article_text:
Films and events

Shorts

As the Years Roll By

In reflecting on the past or embracing unexpected futures, time flows through people’s connection with others and the earth, in these shorts on life in the later years.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Total running time 97min

Programmed by Sky Lewis, Victoria Millington

Content advice This short film programme contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

Agnes

Director-screenwriter Leah Vlemmiks

UK-Canada 2026. 11min

Under pressure from her adult daughter to move and become a live-in babysitter, Agnes finds agency in an unexpected place.

Listen

Director Taliesin Black-Brown

USA 2026. 15min

As his mother slips away as a result of dementia, an Alaskan sound recordist listens for what remains.

Geronto

Director Mark Pluck

Screenwriter Christopher Sherwood

UK 2026. 18min

Late one night, Younger, a man in his 20s, meets Older, a man in his 60s, at a discreet London pub.

All Change

Director-screenwriter Lena Molander

UK 2025. 3min

While talking on a train journey, two men admit to regrets over their friendship.

In the Morning Sun

Director-screenwriter Serville Poblete

Philippines-Canada 2026. 21min

A gentle portrait of aging, migration and memory, inspired by the filmmaker’s desire to preserve the warmth of his parents.

A Grief Encounter

Director-screenwriter James Ashley McLaren

Australia 2026. 12min

A struggling taxidermy artist’s flirtation with a customer takes an interesting turn.

Untitled Woman

Director Camille Summers-Valli

Screenwriters Rosemarie Vind, Camille Summers-Valli

UK 2026. 17min

Dawn is invisible to those around her in a world that favours youth, until she fights back.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

I See Myself

From silent protests and secret ponderings to vocal uprisings and drastic acts, watch people endeavour to carve a bigger space for themselves in a world that’s trying to box them in.

Altered States

Fractured memories and uncertain fates are examined in shorts featuring our unshakeable resolve.

Life / Drawing

A selection of animated shorts exploring what connects us to people, the world around us and, most importantly, ourselves.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Takashi Yamazaki

With Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe

Japan 2026. 135min

Courtesy of Anime Limited

Language Japanese With English subtitles

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 17:30

Audio description

Friday 16 October 17:30

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Japan, 1949. Pilot Kōichi, his wife Noriko and adoptive daughter Akiko are attempting from recover from Godzilla’s recent attacks. But just as everything seems settled, a new danger emerges. Meanwhile, at the bottom of the sea, something is stirring. The first Japanese film to be shot for IMAX, Godzilla Minus Zero combines high-octane thrills with more than a little heart.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Hot Spot

The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI.

Rogue Trooper

Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission.

Wildwood

A forest inhabited by magical beings is the setting for this epic stop-motion saga from LAIKA Studios.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Hirokazu Koreeda

With Natsuki Deguchi, Aju Makita

Japan 2026. 100min

Courtesy of GKIDS

Language Japanese With English subtitles

Introduction

Aspiring manga artist Fujino meets Kymoto, a shy admirer of her work. Seemingly opposites, they create the perfect team with their shared love of the form. But as their work draws praise and attention, they find themselves confronted with decisions that threaten their artistic collaboration. Koreeda’s stiking love letter to friendship and the creative process offers keen insight into the craft.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ana, en passant

Fernanda Salgado’s gorgeous animation is a travelogue of memories, ancestral connections and the future experiences that shape one’s identity.

All of a Sudden

Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s delivers an audiaciously tender, transcendent study of humanity through the subtle account of a life-changing encounter.

Mouse

Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

Too Many Beasts

L’Espece explosive

In this deliciously unhinged mash-up of rural thriller and dark comedy, enormous wild boars create havoc in a small French town.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Sarah Arnold

Screenwriters Sarah Arnold, Jérémie Dubois, Olivier Seror, Romain Winkler, Mehdi Ben Attia

With Alexis Manenti, Ella Rumpf, Vincent Dedienne

France 2026. 95min

Courtesy of Playtime

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Farmers and hunters are openly at war in the rural town of Sérieux. Wild boars are ruining crops and putting everyone on edge. When a local farmer mysteriously disappears, gendarme Fulda is put on the case. As he reluctantly teams up with psychologist Stéphane, the investigation gradually spirals out of control, and so does this offbeat and absurdly funny comedy.

Laure Bonville

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter, drug use, and nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Wild Horse Nine

Martin McDonagh continues to mine the absurdities and complexities of male relationships in a film that brims with energy and is sure to delight.

The History of Concrete

Having attended a Hallmark movie workshop, John Wilson applies his learnings to a documentary about concrete, albeit with a dryly funny and deceptively understated tone.

The Fox

A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy.

content.article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

Fruit Gathering

Writer-director Aung Phyoe’s enthralling, visually striking drama charts a homoerotic friendship between two young Burmese women.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Aung Phyoe

With Nandar Myat Aung, Nandar Myint Lwin

Myanmar-Czechia-France 2026. 79min

Courtesy of Third Floor Production

Language Burmese With English subtitles

Introduction

San Kyi and Theint Theint Oo work in a garment factory in Yangon, formerly the capital of Myanmar. What begins as an innocent encounter between the two young women soon develops into something both delicious and dangerous. Winner of the Crystal Globe at Karlovy Vary International Film Festival, Phyoe’s rich, emotionally enveloping drama intelligently explores the complexities of the women’s relationship.

Wema Mumma

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

Contains themes of self harm.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Filipiñana

This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.

Iván & Hadoum

Ian de la Rosa’s debut, set in a vast greenhouse in southern Spain, is a tender love story that finds newly promoted Iván falling for co-worker Hadoum.

Our Share of Sand

Shalini Adnani’s poignant coming-of-age drama presents a unique perspective on India’s gaping class inequality, child labour and the deep corruption underpinning a family’s economic status.

Films and events

Cult

The Blood Countess

Die BlutGräfin

Isabelle Huppert dazzles as the Blood Countess in this delightful and high-camp gothic fantasy from visionary filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Ulrike Ottinger

With Isabelle Huppert, Birgit Minichmayr, Thomas Schubert

Austria-Luxembourg-Germany 2026. 119min

Courtesy of MAGNIFY

Languages German, French With English subtitles

Introduction

After awakening from a long slumber, the Blood Countess embarks on a quest, with her devoted maid and trusty pet bat in tow, to search for an ancient text that could cause the demise of her vampire realm. Based on the legend of Countess Elizabeth Báthory, Huppert perfectly embodies the role of the bloodthirsty seductress who reigns over present-day Vienna.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Face of Horror

In this stunning, blood-soaked homage to Technicolor horror films, a woman in medieval England rises from the grave to wreak revenge on her husband.

Hot Spot

The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI.

Queens of the Night: Female Vampires on Screen

Step into the seductive, dangerous and ever-evolving world of cinema's most captivating immortal: the female vampire.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Fatherland

In a masterclass of control and precision, Paweł Pawlikowski explores the fragmented soul of postwar Germany through a father-daughter road trip dominated by personal ghosts.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Paweł Pawlikowski

Screenwriters Paweł Pawlikowski, Henk Handloegten

With Sandra Hüller, Hanns Zischler, August Diehl

Poland-Germany-Italy-France 2026. 82min

Courtesy of MUBI

Languages German, English, French, Russian With English subtitles

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 18:15

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Thursday 15 October 15:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 13:20

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In 1949, Erika (a superb Sandra Hüller) is accompanying her father, Nobel laureate author Thomas Mann, on a literary tour through West and East Germany. As family tragedy strikes, it becomes apparent that the spiritual healing Mann deems essential for the divided country may be necessary for their own relationship. It’s an impeccably shot and evocative drama that meditates on the healing process for a fractured national identity.

Diana Cipriano

Content advice

Contains scenes of suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Man of His Time

The banality of evil is brilliantly exposed in this thought-provoking and singular portrait of a mediocre yet ambitious bureaucrat in Nazi-occupied France.

Coward

Lukas Dhont’s latest gem is a luminous and deeply romantic love story, set against the backdrop of the First World War.

Woman Unknown

In May el-Toukhy’s powerful third feature, Marie, a survivor with secrets, navigates retribution and the febrile chaos of life in post-war Denmark.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives

Daniel Oriahi’s wonderful adaptation of Lola Shoneyin’s acclaimed novel is an engrossing exploration of a highly traditional Yoruba household forced to confront hidden truths from its past.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Daniel Oriahi

Screenwriters Adze Ugah, Daniel Oriahi, Heidi Uys, Mo Abudu

With Omowunmi Dada, Iyabo Ojo, Mercy Aigbe, Bimbo Ademoye

Nigeria 2026. 119min

Courtesy of The Baba Segi Collective

Languages Yoruba, English With some English subtitles

Introduction

In this gripping exploration of sexual politics, power and survival in present-day Nigeria, patriarch Baba Segi oversees a household with his three wives, a seemingly harmonious polyamorous arrangement with their children. However, with the arrival of his youngest university educated fourth wife and the revelation that she is unable to conceive, cracks begin to appear in the facade, undermining the dynamics of Segi’s world. Oriahi foregrounds the women’s lives and stories in this compelling film.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex and sexual violence.

Contains themes of abortion.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ben’Imana

This Cannes Camera d’Or winner unfolds in the shadow of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, exploring its legacy and the possibility of forgiveness.

Clarissa

Sophie Okonedo shines in Arie and Chuko Esiri’s (Eyimofe, LFF 2020) sophomore feature film, a delicate, sun-soaked re-imagining of Mrs Dalloway, set in contemporary Lagos.

Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.

Films and events

Family

Relaxed screening: A Mighty Adventure

Relaxed screenings

House lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned down. Audience members will be able to make noise, stim freely, move around or leave and return during the screening.

We will provide a sanctuary space for you to use near the auditorium.

See other screenings of this film

This lovingly crafted, dialogue-free animated tale follows a trio of insects who undertake an epic journey.

Credits

Director-screenwriter Toe Yuen

Taiwan-Malaysia-Hong Kong (S.A.R of China) 2026. 77min

Courtesy of Golden Network Asia

Language Dialogue free

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 18:20

Relaxed screening

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

A butterfly and a grasshopper are removed from the forest and taken to an apartment in the city. Here, they befriend a spider who tries to help them on the long journey back home, which is fraught with dangerous challenges. This innovative and engrossing animated adventure transports us into a familiar world, albeit from the microcosmic perspective of its protagonists.

Justin Johnson

Before the screening

Doors will open 30 minutes before the screening start time.

No trailers will be shown.

The programme will be introduced.

During the screening

Our house lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned slightly down.

You will be able to leave the auditorium and return during the screening.

You will be able to make noise.

We will provide a quiet space for you to use near the auditorium.

You are welcome to take refreshments into the cinema but no hot food please. For information on BFI Bar & Kitchen and BFI Riverfront please see our food and drink page .

How to book

Find out about booking access tickets .

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

Nightborn

A couple’s dream of idyllic family life in the Finnish woods is shattered by the arrival of their nightmarish new baby, in Hanna Bergholm’s riotously gory folk horror.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Hanna Bergholm

Screenwriters Hanna Bergholm, Ilja Rautsi

With Seidi Haarla, Rupert Grint

Finland-Lithuania-France-UK 2026. 92min

Courtesy of Shudder

Languages English, Finnish With some English subtitles

Introduction

Drawing deeply from the wells of folk horror and psychological post-natal angst, director Bergholm pits Seidi Haarla and Rupert Grint’s new parents against their hairy, howling offspring, which displays a taste for raw meat over milk. Gruesome and bloody, it’s also chock-full of self-aware humour that surely guarantees the film’s place as a future cult classic.

Leigh Singer

With thanks to Finnish Institute.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and harm towards children.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Hot Spot

The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI.

The Face of Horror

In this stunning, blood-soaked homage to Technicolor horror films, a woman in medieval England rises from the grave to wreak revenge on her husband.

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Create

Easter

Sekja, an ageing and charismatic Korean trans burlesque star, is front and centre in this glorious film about life.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Mokya Shin

With Saekja, Jinhyo Lim, Rosemary

South Korea 2026. 84min

Courtesy of Low Light Films

Language Korean With English subtitles

Introduction

As the spotlight fades and ornate costumes are put away, Sekja, an elder in the Korean adult entertainment scene, reflects on her life. We are made privy to her thoughts on love, connection and being honest narrators of our own story. Intriguing dance sequences and astonishingly lush aesthetics bring Sekja’s story to life, making Easter a often touching feast of thought and image.

Lynn Nwokorie

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity.

Contains transphobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Sweet Milk Lake

In writer-director-actor Harvey Zielinski’s coming-of-age drama, a young trans man’s homecoming results in unexpected consequences when he’s mistaken for his cisgender twin brother.

Elephants in the Fog

A parent’s search for their missing child disrupts the fragile coexistence between Nepal’s kinnar community and the rest of a village’s population.

I Plant My Hand in the Garden

Playing versions of themselves as the central protagonists, Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija make a daring debut: a witty, irreverent and politically astute portrait of lives shaped by the search for belonging.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

The Unknown

L’Inconnue

Mesmerising, stimulating and unsettling, Niels Schneider and Léa Seydoux star in this body-swap tale that grapples with the existential implications of being trapped inside someone else’s physical being.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Arthur Harari

Screenwriters Arthur Harari, Lucas Harari, Vincent Poymiro

With Léa Seydoux, Niels Schneider

France 2025. 140min

Courtesy of Pathé Films

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

David, a withdrawn photographer, meets a mysterious woman at a party. The two share a sexual encounter, only for David to wake up the morning after in the woman’s body. Arthur Harari’s (co-writer of Anatomy of a Fall) vertiginous, occasionally harrowing and ultimately rewarding ride eschews straightforward resolution in favour of a reflection on the aftermath of severing the link between body and mind.

Diana Cipriano

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, sex, and suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Blood Countess

Isabelle Huppert dazzles as the Blood Countess in this delightful and high-camp gothic fantasy from visionary filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger.

Rogue Trooper

Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission.

Nightborn

A couple’s dream of idyllic family life in the Finnish woods is shattered by the arrival of their nightmarish new baby, in Hanna Bergholm’s riotously gory folk horror.

Films and events

Laugh

The Banning Curse

Nefrin-e Toghif

Iranian director Mohsen Amiryousefi discusses his eventful career with the Angel of Death in this hilarious cinematic autofiction about the highs and lows of radical filmmaking.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Mohsen Amiryousefi

With Mohsen Amiryousefi

Iran 2026. 88min

Courtesy of Irimage

Language Persian With English subtitles

Introduction

After the critical success of his first film at Cannes, Amiryousefi returned to Iran to find it banned by state authorities. It’s a pattern that continued through his entire career, which the seasoned director looks back on in this imaginative, satirical portrait. A balance of biography and constructed fiction, the filmmaker’s own life and Iran’s turbulent political, social and cultural history is entwined via a rich trove of archive footage.

Wema Mumma

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lali

Two emotionally scarred strangers are thrust into an arranged marriage, in this wildly original, pitch-black comedy with hints of the supernatural.

In a Whisper

When a young queer woman returns home to Tunisia to mourn her uncle’s death, she finds his cause of death shrouded in mystery.

Hot Water

This atmospheric and sharply funny road movie sees a Lebanese mother and her American son take a trip, with a lot to unpack along the way.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Hearing

Thính giác

Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Lê Bảo

With Nguyễn Quốc Tuấn, Ngọc Tản, Khánh Huyền

Vietnam-Singapore-Norway-France-Indonesia-Saudi Arabia-Cambodia-Thailand-Taiwan 2026. 128min

Courtesy of Heretic

Language Vietnamese With English subtitles

Introduction

Working as a decibel-reader technician, Ninh encounters hidden sonic tensions within the world around him, from uneasy presences in a cemetery to the restless rhythms of a zoo. Through these encounters, the film transforms the everyday into moments of unexpected drama and tenderness. Utilising his signature style – meticulous framing and minimalist performances – Bảo expands his formalism into an open, emotionally resonant cinematic experience.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra

Jacqueline Lentzou follows Moon 66 Questions with this evocative and playful look into the life of a teenager who is completely unaware of the forces at play in her fate.

Supporting Role

This mysterious and uniquely introspective journey through Tbilisi traces the steps of a once-famous Georgian actor.

The Calf Doll

When his only cow delivers a stillborn calf and then falls sick, a retired professor turns to an age-old calf-doll ritual, while industrialisation closes in around him.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

Mouse

Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors Kelly O’Sullivan, Alex Thompson

Screenwriter Kelly O’Sullivan

With Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Sophie Okonedo, Chloe Coleman

USA 2026. 120min

Courtesy of Altitude

Language English

Introduction

Lifelong friends Callie and Minnie are like ying and yang: one loud and popular, the other shy and quiet. Abruptly forced out from her friend’s shadow, it’s finally time for Minnie to figure out who she is on her own terms. Kupferer and Okonedo’s performances drive this beautiful film that’s guaranteed to have audiences alternating between crying and laughing out loud.

Grace Barber-Plentie

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

7 Miles Out

Carol Morley (Dreams of a Life, The Falling) adapts her moving semi-autobiographical novel, capturing her adolescence in Stockport during the 70s and 80s.

Hot Water

This atmospheric and sharply funny road movie sees a Lebanese mother and her American son take a trip, with a lot to unpack along the way.

Josephine

Winner of the Grand Jury Dramatic Prize at Sundance, this suspenseful and devastating film follows a child trying to navigate life after witnessing a sexual assault.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

The Idiot(s)

Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors Małgorzata Szumowska, Michał Englert

Screenwriters Małgorzata Szumowska, Michał Englert, Kasper Bajon, Brid Arnstein

With Aimee Lou Wood, Johnny Flynn, Vicky Krieps

Germany-Poland 2026. 118min

Courtesy of The Match Factory

Languages English, French, German With English subtitles

Introduction

Anna Dostoevsky loves her husband Fyodor. Fyodor loves his wife, but he also loves gambling and booze. Living in self-imposed exile in Germany, Fyodor’s biggest obstacle to creative progress is himself. Anna tries desperately to rid him of his procrastination so he can deliver a new novel and they can avoid destitution. Sending up the myth of the male genius, The Idiot(s) is also a beautiful love story about the writer and the wife that saved him.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of infant death, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

Possible Love

Lee Chang-dong’s masterfully directed follow-up to Burning (LFF 2018) finds four strangers’ lives entwined by hidden desires and repressed emotions.

The Last Day

Acclaimed visual artist Rachel Rose gives Mrs Dalloway a contemporary makeover in her arresting mood piece, starring Alicia Vikander and Victoria Pedretti.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

Relaxed screening: The History of Concrete

Relaxed screenings

House lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned down. Audience members will be able to make noise, stim freely, move around or leave and return during the screening.

We will provide a sanctuary space for you to use near the auditorium.

See other screenings of this film

Having attended a Hallmark movie workshop, John Wilson applies his learnings to a documentary about concrete, albeit with a dryly funny and deceptively understated tone.

Credits

Director John Wilson

USA 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Visit Films

Language English

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 20:35

Relaxed screening

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

After finding himself with too much time on his hands, documentarian Wilson attends a workshop on how to make Hallmark romcoms. It inspires him to apply the formula to a film investigating the story of concrete. Infused with Wilson’s trademark curiosity and wit, the film project introduces him to a variety of unusual people and places. The result is a wry and humane meditation on the modern world.

Chloé Trayner

Content advice

Contains ableist attitudes and language.

Before the screening

Doors will open 30 minutes before the screening start time.

No trailers will be shown.

The programme will be introduced.

During the screening

Our house lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned slightly down.

You will be able to leave the auditorium and return during the screening.

You will be able to make noise.

We will provide a quiet space for you to use near the auditorium.

You are welcome to take refreshments into the cinema but no hot food please. For information on BFI Bar & Kitchen and BFI Riverfront please see our food and drink page .

How to book

Find out about booking access tickets .

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

content.article_text:
Films and events

Thrill

The Match

Few sporting contests loom as large in the public imagination as the dramatic 1986 World Cup Quarter Final between England and Argentina, as this documentary details.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriters Juan Cabral, Santiago Franco

With Gary Lineker, Jorge Valdano

Argentina-Spain 2026. 91min

Courtesy of Walt Disney Studios

Languages English, Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

England players, including Gary Lineker and John Barnes, assemble with their Argentine counterparts to relive the famed ‘hand of god’ match, which is artfully juxtaposed against the geopolitical conflict that proceeded it. Based on Andrés Burgo’s book, Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco have crafted one of the most thrilling documentaries of the year, infusing history and politics with the excitement and import of this legendary match.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Heysel 85

This is a gripping and sobering dramatic reconstruction of the tragedy that unfolded during the 1985 European Cup final between Liverpool and Juventus at the Brussels stadium.

Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing

Erik Shirai’s beautifully shot and fascinating film grants rare access inside the disciplined inner domain of Japan’s sumo wrestling world.

Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff

This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

A Long Winter

Andrew Haigh’s sensitive drama transforms a snowbound landscape into a space where beauty and longing exist in delicate equilibrium.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Andrew Haigh

With Fred Hechinger, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Caitríona Balfe, Kit Connor, D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai

Canada-UK 2026. 117min

Courtesy of MUBI

Language English

Access information

Thursday 15 October 12:15

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Saturday 17 October 14:30

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 14:45

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Returning to his childhood home deep in Colorado’s mountains, Mike is drawn back into the quiet rituals of family life, as if time had stood still. But when his mother suddenly disappears in the season’s first snowstorm, the familiar order begins to unravel, leaving Mike to negotiate new dynamics with his father as he searches for his own sense of self and belonging. Adapting Brooklyn novelist Colm Tóibín’s short story, Haigh’s (45 Years, All of Us Strangers) intimate drama delicately uncovers hidden fractures within the family, revealing unspoken truths.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Man I Love

Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

The Idiot(s)

Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

It Gets Worse

Leo Reich’s new series turns the struggles of young Londoners into its playground, mining a generation’s problems for biting, clever comedy.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Episodes 1-3

Series Creator Leo Reich

Director Mounia Akl

Screenwriter Leo Reich

With Leo Reich, Emily Fairn, Olive Gray

UK 2026. 69min

Courtesy of Channel 4

Language English

Introduction

Ethan, Abi and Sam, inseparable friends in their mid-20s, are forced into real adulthood when eviction looms. Razor-sharp and witty, It Gets Worse skewers a generation stuck between housing crisis, humiliating jobs and messy relationships, while savouring the joy of youth in one of the buzziest cities in the world. It’s anchored by standout performances from the three leads, alongside unforgettable cameos from the likes of Lena Dunham and Andrew Scott.

Claire Nicolas

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

Contains scenes of drug use, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Club Kid

A jaded New York club promoter finds his messy lifestyle upended by the discovery that he has a son, in Jordan Firstman’s hilarious feature directorial debut.

I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

In Clio Barnard’s poignant drama, five childhood friends from Birmingham find their lifelong bonds tested as adulthood brings fractured relationships, unfulfilled dreams and long-buried secrets to light.

The Trip to the Northern Lights

Rob Brydon and Steve Coogan are back on the road, sharing delicious meals, hilarious banter and celebrity impressions as they journey through northern Europe.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

Rebellion

Revolution is the beat that drums through this electrifying story about the landmark case against the Bradford 12.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriters Ken Fero, Tariq Mehmood

UK 2026. 80min

Courtesy of Migrant Media

Language English

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 20:50

Descriptive subtitles

Thursday 15 October 13:50

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In 1981, 12 young Asian men stood trial on terrorism charges for defending Bradford from an imminent racist attack. Their fight for their city – and their freedom – became international news, awakening public consciousness to the rise of fascism and the far-right. Activist-filmmaker Ken Fero’s (Ultraviolence, LFF 2020) documentary plays out as a revolutionary and all-too-timely blueprint for the battle against political violence.

Lynn Nwokorie

Content advice

Contains scenes of racism, racist attitudes and language, and racist violence.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Tracing Islands

These films invite reflection on places that remember, histories that persist, and cinema’s role in unearthing hidden relationships between ecology, extractive capitalism and collective survival.

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

The second part of Julia Loktev’s epic documentary, detailing the persecution of journalists in Russia, follows her brave protagonists’ escape abroad following the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Campaigns for Justice: From the Bradford 12 to Today

Join us for a conversation that reflects on both past and present-day community activism in the fight against racism and injustice.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Create

Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff

This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Nanette Burstein

USA 2026. 90min

Courtesy of National Geographic

Language English

Access information

Friday 16 October 21:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Carl Sagan dedicated his life to understanding the universe and our place within it, inspiring millions of people to become more interested in worlds beyond our own. Drawing on archives and interviewing those closest to him, this touching tribute interweaves Sagan’s pioneering research – and boundless passion for activism and advocacy – with his complex private life and the personal and working relationship that would define his later life.

Chloé Trayner

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Perfect Road

By turns exhilarating and intimate, this documentary portrait charts nomadic cyclist Max Schnell’s attempt to complete an extreme journey through some of Europe’s highest mountain passes.

Concrete Turned to Sand

Shaped by the tidal rhythms of British Columbia’s oyster farms, this richly cinematic documentary, shot on 35mm, exists where labour, scientific inquiry and the living world meet.

Chronovisor

The film collective Cosmic Salon (Jack Auen and Kevin Walker) make their beguiling and assured feature debut, guiding us through hidden histories and uncanny landscapes of belief, mystery and the unknown.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

Glaxo

An act of betrayal between a close group of friends has terrible consequences in Benjamín Naishtat’s atmospheric period noir.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Benjamín Naishtat

With Lali Espósito, Marcelo Subiotto, Esteban Bigliardi

Brazil-Argentina 2026. 107min

Courtesy of Luxbox Films

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

Four young men in the provincial Argentine city of Chivilcoy find their lives disrupted when a retired police officer and his glamorous young wife move into the area. Add two visiting American Mormons into the mix, along with a volatile political situation, and tensions soon escalate. Pitch-perfect performances and a lush score by Japanese composer Shigeru Umebayashi further distinguish Naishtat’s impressively taut drama.

Maria Delgado

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal cruelty, homophobia, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Life of Jorge Luis Borges

Mariano Llinás’ epic contemplation of the life and works of Jorge Luis Borges is every bit as wily and playful as the Argentine writer’s stories.

Moonglow

The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.

Prince

The stakes are high for a prize-winning show dog, his owner, her butler and their extended family, in this kitsch comedy about avarice and love.

Introduction

Cousins, the creator of the groundbreaking The Story of Film: A New Generation and Women Make Film, trains his distinctive film-historian lens on the evolution of documentary. The result is a rich tapestry of landmark works and underappreciated gems. In this illuminating chapter, he guides us through the 1990s, a decade of filmmakers exploring bodies, spirituality, labour, war and politics, against the backdrop of rising commercial interest in the form.

Chloé Trayner

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Act 3

The latest in Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor’s series of cinematic essays is a rich and thought-provoking journey through ageing, legacy and the intersection between artistic and personal relationships.

Dependence

A filmmaker sifts through decades of home movies to understand her father, in this intimate study of what it means to love an addict.

Mark Cousins: The Story of Documentary Film

Acclaimed filmmaker and writer Mark Cousins joins us for a fascinating exploration of documentary cinema.

Films and events

Galas

The Beloved

El ser querido

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Rodrigo Sorogoyen

Screenwriters Rodrigo Sorogoyen, Isabel Peña

With Javier Bardem, Victoria Luengo, Raúl Arévalo

Spain 2026. 135min

Courtesy of Curzon

Languages Spanish, English With some English subtitles

Introduction

Esteban is an Oscar-winning director. His daughter Emilia a struggling actor. He returns to Spain to make a film about the country’s exploitation of Western Sahara and offers her the lead role. The film shoot that follows isn’t a straightforward experience, demonstrating the unresolved tensions that still haunt their relationship. Guilt, resentment and forgiveness all intersect to powerful effect in this tense drama.

Maria Delgado

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Bunker

Set against a backdrop of widening class divisions and capitalist excess, Florian Zeller’s elegantly crafted psychological thriller is anchored by magnificent performances from Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

La Bola Negra

A genre-defying queer epic, rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, this is majestic and original filmmaking.

Behemoth!

Michael Clayton director Tony Gilroy returns with a stylishly crafted portrait of a beguiling classical musician, played by Pedro Pascal.

content.article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

ANIMOL

Ashley Walters’ directorial debut, set in a young offenders institute, is a strikingly shot and sensitively made depiction of survival, surprise connections and redemption.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Ashley Walters

Screenwriter Nick Love

With Tut Nyuot, Vladyslav Baliuk, Stephen Graham

UK 2025. 92min

Courtesy of Sky

Language English

Access information

Sunday 11 October 18:25

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Thursday 15 October 12:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 21:00

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

On arriving behind bars, Troy quickly comes into the orbit of two people who will define his life inside: dominant kingpin Dion and wisecracking Krystiyan. Will these relationships help him survive, or bring about his downfall? Having already carved out a career as one of the UK’s most talented actors, Walters now emerges as an exciting filmmaking voice.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use and graphic violence or injury.

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Place to Heal

Cédric Kahn’s watchful drama deftly captures life within an adolescent psychiatric unit, from the carers’ work to the kids’ trauma, friendships and lust for life.

In the Shadows

Jasmine Jobson leads a brilliant ensemble in bringing the inspirational story of champion East End boxer Ramla Ali to the screen.

FLORID

In this striking British feature debut, a young man living in supported accommodation tries to juggle his musical aspirations and mental health issues.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Bunker

Set against a backdrop of widening class divisions and capitalist excess, Florian Zeller’s elegantly crafted psychological thriller is anchored by magnificent performances from Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Florian Zeller

With Javier Bardem, Penélope Cruz, Stephen Graham, Paul Dano, Patrick Schwarzenegger

UK 2026. 126min

Courtesy of STUDIOCANAL

Languages Spanish, English With English subtitles

Introduction

After 17 years of marriage, the seemingly stable lives of an acclaimed architect and his publisher wife begin to unravel when he accepts a controversial commission to build a luxury bunker for a tech billionaire. With an impeccable sense of atmosphere and pacing, this intense character study from the writer-director of The Son (LFF 2022) and The Father evolves into an unsettling moral puzzle where desire, privilege and paranoia collide.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Beloved

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.

Possible Love

Lee Chang-dong’s masterfully directed follow-up to Burning (LFF 2018) finds four strangers’ lives entwined by hidden desires and repressed emotions.

La Bola Negra

A genre-defying queer epic, rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, this is majestic and original filmmaking.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

Hot Spot

The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Agnieszka Smoczyńska

Screenwriter Robert Bolesto

With Andrzej Konopka, Noomi Rapace, Reika Kirishima

Poland-Greece 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Focus Features

Languages English, Japanese, Polish With some English subtitles

Access information

Saturday 10 October 21:00

Audio description

Monday 12 October 18:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Thursday 15 October 13:30

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Djonny, a vibrantly dressed private eye, is called to solve a mysterious murder case, only to discover a rebel group capable of undermining the digital overlord led by Rana, who may or may not be a cyber witch. Agnieszka Smoczyńska creates a hypnotic, dystopian world that lures you in with its breathtaking aesthetics and hallucinatory images.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Too Many Beasts

In this deliciously unhinged mash-up of rural thriller and dark comedy, enormous wild boars create havoc in a small French town.

Tropical Fractals

Leonardo Pirondi’s timely reflection on ecological collapse imagines a future in which a biodome spaceship preserves the last traces of life on Earth.

Chronovisor

The film collective Cosmic Salon (Jack Auen and Kevin Walker) make their beguiling and assured feature debut, guiding us through hidden histories and uncanny landscapes of belief, mystery and the unknown.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

The Slightest Touch

The power of friendship and connection is explored in Rachel Fleit’s soulful and life-affirming documentary, featuring Emma Fogarty and Colin Farrell.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Rachel Fleit

USA-Ireland 2026. 103min

Courtesy of HBO Max

Language English

Access information

Monday 12 October 20:45

Descriptive subtitles

Thursday 15 October 16:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Emma lives with Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), the slightest touch causing her skin to blister and tear. To celebrate her 40th, she runs a marathon with longtime pal, Colin, raising awareness of this shamefully understudied condition. Defying the odds with grit and humour, this dynamic duo’s race to the finish is an inspirational ode to friendship and being open to the world and all that it offers.

Kristy Matheson

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Being Heumann

British actor Ruth Madeley is outstanding as Judith Heumann, the activist who helped fight for anti-discrimination laws for individuals with disabilities, in CODA director Siân Heder’s enthralling film.

Adam Pearson: Zero Intention of Living Quietly

Actor, broadcaster, and leading disability advocate Adam Pearson joins us to discuss his career and his influential advocacy work for more inclusive storytelling and authentic representation.

Petrolheads

Life can feel like a Western in this warm buddy movie, in which neurodiverse Martin and Casper search for their perfect car: the 1994 Honda Civic.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

Act 3

The latest in Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor’s series of cinematic essays is a rich and thought-provoking journey through ageing, legacy and the intersection between artistic and personal relationships.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriters Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor

Ireland-UK 2026. 83min

Courtesy of Desperate Optimists

Language English

Access information

Thursday 15 October 17:00

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Molloy and Lawlor (Baltimore, LFF 2023) engage in a witty and moving conversation that explores family history and their latest project, a film about groundbreaking artists Claude Cahun and Marcel Moore. As they analyse this decades-long relationship, they identify parallels between these two artists and their own lives. Act 3 celebrates the power of connection, artistic exploration and the importance of memory to shape our present and future.

Grace Barber-Plentie

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

content.article_text:
Films and events

Thrill

Moonglow

The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Isabel Sandoval

With Isabel Sandoval, Arjo Atayde

Philippines-Taiwan-Japan 2026. 108min

Courtesy of Film Republic

Language Filipino With English subtitles

Introduction

When Dahlia commits a high-profile robbery, the last person she expected to be investigating her is Charlie, an ex-lover from more than a decade ago. Years later, their connection still sparks. But what will happen when Charlie learns the truth? Expertly directed and acted by Isabel Sandoval, who plays with the conventions of noir, Moonglow is a feast for the senses.

Grace Barber-Plentie

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Elephants in the Fog

A parent’s search for their missing child disrupts the fragile coexistence between Nepal’s kinnar community and the rest of a village’s population.

The Dreamed Adventure

Featuring a vibrant lead performance, this gripping realist drama, set in a lawless town on the Bulgaria-Turkey border, exudes an atmosphere of danger and paranoia.

My Notes on Mars

In Lili Horvát’s beguiling third feature, the sudden return of Sam’s missing wife, who has no memory of anything except her scientific research, gives their relationship another chance.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Tender Loving Care

In a world that feels increasingly untethered from human connection, the incomparable Mike Leigh returns with a thought-provoking and compassionate view of urban life.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Mike Leigh

With Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson

UK 2026. 107min

Courtesy of STUDIOCANAL

Language English

Access information

Thursday 15 October 18:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Saturday 17 October 12:15

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 13:05

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

In contemporary London, social workers Amy and Rosie navigate the stressors and joys of life together, be that work, family or messy dating lives. Leigh and his tight ensemble – Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson – breathe life into these characters with a deep naturalism that illuminates life’s complexities with warmth, humour and much-needed kindness.

Kristy Matheson

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ink

Danny Boyle brings a seismic moment in Rupert Murdoch’s Fleet Street career blazingly to life, employing the breathtaking style of a story torn from the headlines.

I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

In Clio Barnard’s poignant drama, five childhood friends from Birmingham find their lifelong bonds tested as adulthood brings fractured relationships, unfulfilled dreams and long-buried secrets to light.

In the Shadows

Jasmine Jobson leads a brilliant ensemble in bringing the inspirational story of champion East End boxer Ramla Ali to the screen.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

The Face of Horror

In this stunning, blood-soaked homage to Technicolor horror films, a woman in medieval England rises from the grave to wreak revenge on her husband.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Anna Biller

With Jonah Hauer-King, Kristine Froseth, Ellie Bamber

UK 2026. 120min

Courtesy of Embankment Films

Language English

Introduction

Returning as a ghost after a cruel betrayal results in her death, Eleanor and her sister deliver bloody vengeance on the man who took her life and murdered their father. Anna Biller, writer-director of The Love Witch, here delivers a rich visual feast. Gloriously shot on 35mm, this supernatural Gothic melodrama vibrantly brings 14th-century England to life.

Victoria Millington

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, self-harm, and sexual violence.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Blood Countess

Isabelle Huppert dazzles as the Blood Countess in this delightful and high-camp gothic fantasy from visionary filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger.

Nightborn

A couple’s dream of idyllic family life in the Finnish woods is shattered by the arrival of their nightmarish new baby, in Hanna Bergholm’s riotously gory folk horror.

Rogue Trooper

Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

It Will Happen Tonight

Succederà Questa Notte

Renowned Italian filmmaker Nanni Moretti returns to our screens with this gloriously funny romantic fantasy about the separate lives of two people meant for each other.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Nanni Moretti

Screenwriters Nanni Moretti, Federica Pontremoli, Vania Santella

With Louis Garrel, Jasmine Trinca, Hippolyte Girardot

Italy-France-Spain 2026. 103min

Courtesy of Playtime

Languages Italian, Spanish, French With English subtitles

Introduction

A chance encounter between two people whose destinies appear entwined soon sees them separated, then reunited accidentally, occasionally and unwittingly. This comic romantic fantasy is played with panache and no small amount of charm by Louis Garrel and Jasmine Trinca, with Moretti bringing his signature heart, wit and intelligence to the enterprise.

Adrian Wootton

With thanks to Cinecittà.

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

Contains sexist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ketticè

Following his debut Diciannove (LFF 2024), Giovanni Tortorici continues his collaboration with producer Luca Guadagnino on this vibrant coming-of-age story, set in early 2000s Palermo.

A Common Story

Anna Foglietta’s beautifully observed and impressively directed feature debut details the fractures that appear in a couple’s seemingly happy marriage.

The Echo Chamber

Andrea Pallaoro’s take on an unfilmed Bertolucci script is a frank portrait of a famous music producer whose life spirals dangerously out of control.
