content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

I Love Boosters

The writer-director behind Sorry to Bother You (LFF 2018) is back with another idiosyncratic, anti-capitalist vision, featuring an all-star cast that includes Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, LaKeith Stanfield and Demi Moore.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Boots Riley

With Keke Palmer, Demi Moore, Naomi Ackie, Taylour Paige, LaKeith Stanfield

USA 2026. 113min

Courtesy of Universal Pictures

Language English

Certificate BBFC18

Access information

Friday 9 October 21:15

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Thursday 15 October 18:10

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 20:45

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Corvette is an aspiring fashion designer and leader of The Velvet Gang, a group of ‘boosters’ who rob clothes from fashion entrepreneur Christie Smith’s boutiques. But when Smith steals one of Corvette’s designs, The Velvet Gang are pushed to the next level. Boots Riley’s film is a wild fashion fever dream and a rally cry against the system.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Screen Talk: Naomi Ackie

We welcome Naomi Ackie, who is appearing in I Love Boosters in the festival, to this Screen Talk to discuss her career.

Wicker

Olivia Colman gives yet another bravura performance in this delightfully offbeat comedy, playing an outcast from her village who orders herself a wicker husband.

Klara and the Sun

Oscar winner Taika Waititi’s luminous adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s bestselling novel sees Jenna Ortega play an enthusiastic artificial friend desperate to find a loving home.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Thrill

Heysel 85

This is a gripping and sobering dramatic reconstruction of the tragedy that unfolded during the 1985 European Cup final between Liverpool and Juventus at the Brussels stadium.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Teodora Ana Mihai

Screenwriters Lode Desmet, Isabelle Darras, Teodora Ana Mihai

With Violet Braeckman, Matteo Simoni, Josse De Pauw

Belgium-Netherlands-Germany 2026. 92min

Courtesy of Icon Film Distribution

Languages Dutch, French, English, Italian With English subtitles

Certificate BBFC12A

Introduction

Teodora Ana Mihai rightly leaves the match off screen to focus on the ordeal endured by hundreds of fans. The film also channels its outrage at events that live television had no access to: the sloppy pre-match planning, the slow response and pathetic handling of the catastrophe and the irresponsible power play that shaped those dreadful, fateful hours.

Sergio Fant

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Match

Few sporting contests loom as large in the public imagination as the dramatic 1986 World Cup Quarter Final between England and Argentina, as this documentary details.

The Meltdown

Sutherland Award winner Manuela Martelli delivers a knife-edge thriller centring on the disappearance of a teenager in a remote Chilean resort.

Black Church Bay

In a sleepy Welsh fishing village, Barry’s life starts to unravel after an intimate encounter in this gripping mystery drama starring Tom Cullen and Joe Locke.

Films and events

Thrill

Black Church Bay

In a sleepy Welsh fishing village, Barry’s life starts to unravel after an intimate encounter in this gripping mystery drama starring Tom Cullen and Joe Locke.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Rhys Marc Jones

With Tom Cullen, Joe Locke, Marli Siu

UK 2026. 107min

Courtesy of Vertigo Releasing Ltd

Language English

Access information

Thursday 15 October 18:30

Audio description

Saturday 17 October 12:45

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Barry has always kept his personal life tightly under wraps. But as hidden truths come to light, he is no longer able to control the double life he leads. Barry must decide what lengths he will go to cover up his private life and ultimately his true self. Black Church Bay is a tense and thought-provoking drama that affirms Rhys Marc Jones as an exciting queer filmmaker.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Moonglow

The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.

A Long Winter

Andrew Haigh’s sensitive drama transforms a snowbound landscape into a space where beauty and longing exist in delicate equilibrium.

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

Dao

The new film by Alain Gomis is a formally inventive, politically attuned meditation on the enduring ties of the African diaspora, and the meaning of family and community.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Alain Gomis

With Katy Correa, D’Johé Kouadio, Samir Guesmi

France-Senegal-Guinea-Bissau 2026. 185min

Courtesy of The Party Film Sales

Languages French, Manjak, Wolof, Creole Portuguese With English subtitles

Introduction

Moving between a memorial ritual in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in France, Dao brings these two rites of passage into intimate conversation, exploring diasporic lives shaped by distance, memory and belonging. Blending fictional narrative with interviews and rehearsal scenes with its performers, Gomis creates a warm, richly layered, jazz-inflected portrait in which lived experience and performance continually illuminate one another.

Hyun Jin Cho

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

House of the Wind

Cameroonian director Bernard Auguste Kouemo Yanghu’s outstanding feature debut is a poignant tale of an ageing parent who has been left behind.

Masc

Bertil Nilsson’s distinctive debut follows Robin as he moves through temporary jobs and tentative relationships in search of a place to belong.

Let Them Be Seen

Nolitha Refilwe Mkulisi’s debut feature – a tender love letter to Tapoleng, her hometown in South Africa – offers an intimate evocation of a community in transition.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

La Bola Negra

A genre-defying queer epic, rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, this is majestic and original filmmaking.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Directors Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo

Screenwriters Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi, Alberto Conejero

With Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Penélope Cruz

Spain-France 2026. 155min

Courtesy of Altitude

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

Spain, 1932. A young man awaits to see if he has secured membership of the local casino. In 1937, a young nationalist soldier guards a republican prisoner. Jump to 2017 and an unexpected document is inherited by an historian from his grandfather. These timelines and a breathtaking cinematic audacity shapes this dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych about communication, inheritance, silence and memory.

Maria Delgado

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Bunker

Set against a backdrop of widening class divisions and capitalist excess, Florian Zeller’s elegantly crafted psychological thriller is anchored by magnificent performances from Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

The Beloved

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.

The Man I Love

Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

Coward

Lukas Dhont’s latest gem is a luminous and deeply romantic love story, set against the backdrop of the First World War.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Lukas Dhont

Screenwriters Lukas Dhont, Angelo Tijssens

With Emmanuel Macchia, Valentin Campagne

Belgium-France-Netherlands 2026. 127min

Courtesy of MUBI

Languages French, Dutch With English subtitles

Certificate LFF18

Access information

Thursday 15 October 20:30

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 15:25

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Quiet young farmer Pierre arrives on the battlefield to discover the horror of trench warfare. His ray of light is a cabaret run by the alluring Francis, who brings life, songs and the unexpected possibility of passionate love. Propelled by magnetic performances and enchanting musical acts, Coward demonstrates how art and desire illuminate dark and brutal times.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Rose

Sandra Hüller gives an award-winning performance as a 17th-century female soldier who disguises herself as a man to gain acceptance in a brutal farming community.

A Man of His Time

The banality of evil is brilliantly exposed in this thought-provoking and singular portrait of a mediocre yet ambitious bureaucrat in Nazi-occupied France.

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Love

In a Whisper

À Voix basse

When a young queer woman returns home to Tunisia to mourn her uncle’s death, she finds his cause of death shrouded in mystery.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Leyla Bouzid

With Eya Bouteraa, Hiam Abbass, Marion Barbeau

France-Tunisia 2026. 113min

Courtesy of Playtime

Languages Arabic, French With English subtitles

Introduction

Returning to her intergenerational matriarchal household, Lilia notices everyone – including herself – is keeping secrets. But as she pries into what happened to her uncle, she must decide if she is finally ready to reveal parts of herself to her loved ones. Leyla Bouzid’s latest film is a sumptuous family drama about lineage and queerness.

Grace Barber-Plentie

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Sweet Milk Lake

In writer-director-actor Harvey Zielinski’s coming-of-age drama, a young trans man’s homecoming results in unexpected consequences when he’s mistaken for his cisgender twin brother.

Ben’Imana

This Cannes Camera d’Or winner unfolds in the shadow of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, exploring its legacy and the possibility of forgiveness.

Fruit Gathering

Writer-director Aung Phyoe’s enthralling, visually striking drama charts a homoerotic friendship between two young Burmese women.

Films and events

Galas

Klara and the Sun

Oscar winner Taika Waititi’s luminous adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s bestselling novel sees Jenna Ortega play an enthusiastic artificial friend desperate to find a loving home.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Taika Waititi

Screenwriters Taika Waititi, Dahvi Waller

With Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Mia Tharia, Steve Buscemi, Natasha Lyonne

New Zealand-USA-UK 2026. 116min

Courtesy of Sony Pictures Releasing UK

Language English

Certificate BBFC12A

Access information

Thursday 15 October 20:45

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Friday 16 October 14:45

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 15:20

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Klara is chosen by Josie to be her friend and takes on the responsibility of bringing joy into the girl’s life. It’s not an easy task, considering Josie’s complicated condition and her fraught relationship with her domineering mother (a superb Amy Adams). Waititi’s distinctive vision perfectly complements Ishiguro’s poignant tale, which explores what it means to be a sentient human being, even if you aren’t one.

Isabel Moir

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

I Love Boosters

The writer-director behind Sorry to Bother You (LFF 2018) is back with another idiosyncratic, anti-capitalist vision, featuring an all-star cast that includes Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, LaKeith Stanfield and Demi Moore.

VisionQuest

Paul Bettany returns as Vision in this highly anticipated follow-up to Marvel’s WandaVision.

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Paula Delsol

With Jacqueline Vandal, Paulette Dubost, Pierre Barouh

France 1964. 83min

Courtesy of Janus Films

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Jacquie, a beautiful 20-year-old, experiences various encounters with men in the south of France, where she returns to her family after leaving Paris. A young woman becoming the target of male predators is always a relevant topic. It’s presented here with a fresh approach: Jacquie is an unburdened wanderer rather than a desperate one, and her search for independence inebriating and joyful.

Giulia Saccogna

Restored in 4K in 2026 by La Cinémathèque française in collaboration with CNC – Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée at TransPerfect Media laboratory, from the original 35mm picture and sound negatives. Funding provided by Neuflize OBC Corporate Foundation.

Content advice

Contains scenes of domestic violence or abuse.

Contains sexist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Pakeezah

One of the last great classical musicals of Indian cinema, the visually opulent and emotionally tragic Pakeezah is a byzantine story of star-crossed lovers.

Gone to Earth

Long overshadowed within Powell and Pressburger’s canon, this major new restoration reveals the visual splendour and dramatic intensity of one of their most misunderstood films.

Ken Russell’s The Devils

Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Create

Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall

One Battle After Another director Paul Thomas Anderson creates an intimate document of Geese frontman Cameron Winter’s solo piano performance at the legendary New York concert hall.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Paul Thomas Anderson

With Cameron Winter

USA 2026. 71min

Courtesy of MUBI

Language English

Introduction

In December 2025, Paul Thomas Anderson collaborated with fellow filmmaker Benny Safdie on a multi-perspective and multi-format recording of Winter’s solo performance. The warm hues capture the feeling in the room, including audience reactions, to create an immersive cinematic experience for those of us who couldn’t be there. It’s a rapturous celebration of live performance, whose appeal should reach far beyond the band and Winter’s existing fan base.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Rules

The Series competition rewards outstanding projects and narrative excellence. Photographers must submit a minimum of five (5) and a maximum of ten (10) images and all submissions must be accompanied by a series description.

If you enter the Series competition, you can also enter the Single Image competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

1.1 By entering the Competition, You agree and acknowledge that the World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive your registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation by its Privacy Policy.

1.2.1 The Competition is free to enter.

1.2.2 The Series competition is open to all Photographers entering a body of work.

1.3 All Entrants must be over 18.

1.4 By entering the Competition You hereby accept these Competition Rules and the Terms and Conditions.

1.5 Entries must be submitted by 12 January, 2027 at 16.00 GMT

1.6 If you enter the Series competition, you can also enter the Single Image competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

2. To enter, you must upload your image via the World Photography Organisation website ( www.worldphoto.org ) or any of the official Sony World Photography Awards’ website and follow the on-screen instructions carefully.

2.1 Image Entry criteria:

Published work may have been taken at any point in history, but must have been published between the dates of 1 January 2026 and 12 January 2027.

Up to 20% of work can be published at any point in time on your personal website, social media or exhibited as part of an official programme i.e. two images can be published on personal platforms at any point in time if submitting a series of 8-10 images. One image can be published at any point in time if submitting a series of 5-7 images.

Un-published work entered into the competition may have been taken at any point in history but never been shown publicly. Once unpublished work has been entered, it cannot be entered again as published work in the future year of the Awards’ competition.

2.2 Images should be no smaller than 1MB and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files.

All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model and EXIF data must be left in the image file.

All Entrants, if they are selected amongst the shortlist, must be able to supply a high resolution image suitable for printing in exhibitions should the image be required.

3.1 Entries will be judged between January 13, 2027 and January 31, 2027.

3.2 The three finalists (1st, 2nd and 3rd place) and a shortlist of up to seven photographers from each category will be selected and announced prior to April 2027. Category winners and overall competition winners will be announced in April 2027. The finalists and shortlist will be notified by email in January.

3.3.1 The winner of each category will be notified by email

3.4 The decision of the Judges and the World Photography Organisation is final and no negotiation will be entered into with respect to any such decision.

3.5 You may enter a minimum of five (5) and a maximum of ten (10) images per category, and may enter as many categories as you wish, however you cannot enter the same series or images into more than one category.

3.5.1 Judging will be based on the portfolio of work entered for each category.

3.5.2. During the judging process successful entries may be moved to a different category to the category they originally entered into. The decision will be made at the discretion of the judging panel. Successful entrants will be notified of the change over email.

4. Your Entry may feature manipulation, but where Entries are manipulated, the extent of which must be described in the image description section when submitting. For the avoidance of doubt, all Entries must originally be from either an analogue or digital photograph which may have then been manipulated. Computer generated content cannot be the origin of the Entry. Should a question arise through the judging process regarding the extent of your Entry’s manipulation you may be requested to submit the original photograph and image file to verify.

4.1 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to disqualify and remove any entry that does not comply with the following requirements, even after the entry is submitted on the Website. You warrant and represent, in respect of each entry submitted by You (“Entry”), as follows:

4.1.1 You are the sole owner and author of each Entry

4.1.2 You have the right to make Your Entry available to the Competition

4.1.3 Each Entry does not contain personally identifiable information about you or any other person(s)

4.1.4 Each Entry does not contain any infringing, threatening, false, misleading, abusive, harassing, libellous,defamatory, vulgar, obscene, scandalous, inflammatory, pornographic or profane content

4.1.5 Each Entry does not contain any material that could constitute or encourage conduct that would be considered a criminal offence, give rise to civil liability, or otherwise violate any law

4.1.6 Each Entry does not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, contract rights, or any other intellectual property rights of any third person or entity, or violate any person’s rights of privacy or publicity, including:

4.1.6.1 trademarks owned by third parties

4.1.6.2 copyrighted materials owned by third parties (including movie dialogue or musical compositions)

4.1.6.3 names, likenesses, voices or other characteristics identifying celebrities or other public figures, living or dead

4.1.7 Entries which contain any commercial content that promotes any product or service other than that of the World Photography Organisation.

4.1.8 Entries containing screen credits

4.1.9 No animals were harmed, manipulated or distressed in the making of the image. This includes, but is not limited to:

Deliberately disturbing or provoking an animal to capture a reaction

Using tape lures or decoys to attract animals or trigger a behaviour

Live baiting of any kind

Using flash photography on nocturnal birds

Failing to adhere to applicable laws, rules and permissions when working with wildlife and in natural environments, for example with protected species or protected environments

4.1.10 Archival images may be used when creating new work where any usage maintains compliance with clause 2. All archival images must be used with the required permissions. Usage of archival images must be stated in the description. 4.1.11 Drone usage must comply with the laws, rules, and permissions of the country in which the image was taken. The Promoter may request proof of permissions where applicable.

4.2 You agree to fully indemnify the World Photography Organisation in respect of all royalties, fees and any other monies owing to any person by reason of Your breaching any of the foregoing.

4.3 You confirm that each person depicted in the Entry has granted permission to be portrayed as shown. Any costumes, props or other materials used must be rented or borrowed with the permission of the owner, and all other relevant permissions must have been obtained.

4.4 In accordance with clause 3.2 and 3.3 all shortlisted and winning photographers will be contacted by email. If the World Photography Organisation does not hear from the entrant by the date specified in any correspondence and is therefore not able to ratify the entry that entrant will be disqualified and replaced by another photographer.

5. Intentionally deleted.

6. The World Photography Organisation may run an online rating process whereby members of the public may vote for a favourite photograph. If there is sufficient evidence (in the World Photography Organisation’s sole discretion) to suggest malpractice and manipulation of the rating process, then the World Photography Organisation has the right to remove the relevant Entry or Entries and, if necessary, award the prize to a different Entrant. The decisions of the World Photography Organisation are final.

7.1 The World Photography Organisation recognises You, the author of the image, retain full ownership of the copyright in each Entry.

7.2 All Entrants understand that any image submitted to the Competition may be used by the World Photography Organisation, and its Event Partners, for marketing and promotional purposes of You the author and the Event only, for a maximum of three years after April 2027. Please refer to clause 7.4. You hereby grant the World Photography Organisation a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence in each Entry throughout the world for three years in all media for any use connected to the promotion of You the author and the Sony World Photography Awards Event and/or Competition, including, but not limited too:

(a) judging the Competition

(b) displaying the winning and shortlisted entries at public exhibitions promoting the World Photography Organisation and organised by the World Photography Organisation

(c) inclusion within the Website, a World Photography Awards book, magazine or similar

(d) inclusion within any materials promoting of the Competition and / or any exhibition organised by the World Photography Organisation, in the promotion of the World Photography Organisation

(e) inclusion on Competition- and exhibition-related products to be sold by the World Photography Organisation or any third party following the individual agreement by the author

(f) sub-licensing the Entries to the press for reproduction in connection with the Competition and any exhibition

(g) allowing viewers of the Website to view images on a computer screen, PDA or mobile telephone and store such pages in electronic form on disk or on a PDA or mobile telephone (but not on any server or other storage device connected to a network) for their personal, non-commercial use only. Please also refer to clause 9.

7.3 All Entrants understand that the image information, including image name and description, may be shared with Event Partners and media as per clause 7.1, 7.2 and 8. For the avoidance of doubt the “image information” does not include any personal information of You the author.

7.3.1 Should entrants elect to opt-in to sharing data, the email data and name will be shared with our event partners.

7.4 For media purposes in accordance with clause 7.2 and to promote your winning images the World Photography Organisation will choose a maximum of two to three images, from the series entered for media use; should media require further images for publication this will be done in consultation with You.

7.5 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right to select which images from within the winning series that will be featured within the curated exhibit and such curation is made in its sole discretion. Associated series descriptions, image captions and bios may also be edited to fit within the context of the exhibition, book or other material connected to the Awards .

7.6 All entrants are required to enter under their correct names, and all entrants are responsible for providing this information accurately. The Awards programme is structured around providing opportunities and exposure to individual photographers and as such we do not award anonymously or accept pseudonyms.

7.7 For Entrants that qualify for the National & Regional Award programme, the Promoter reserves the right not to award a winner if, in the opinion of the judges, none of the Entrants meet the required standard.

8. Any photograph used by the World Photography Organisation shall carry a credit line. Any failure to provide such credit line shall not be deemed to be a breach, as long as the World Photography Organisation uses its reasonable endeavours to rectify such failure within a reasonable period from the date of notice of such failure.

8a. All entrants understand the World Photography Organisation may need to crop your image or add text or logos when used specifically to promote your work or the Awards for online promotional purposes only.

9. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete information, whether caused by website users or by any of the equipment or programming associated with or utilised in the Competition, and the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for technical, hardware or software failure of any kind, for lost network connections, garbled computer transmissions, other problems or technical malfunctions with regard to the Competition. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any error, omission, corruption, interruption, deletion, defect, delay in operation or transmission, communications line failure, theft or destruction or unauthorized access to or alteration of Entries. The World Photography Organisation is not responsible for any problems or technical malfunction of any telephone network or lines, computer on-line systems, servers, computer equipment, software, failure of any e-mail addressed to the World Photography Organisation on account of technical problems, human error or traffic congestion on the internet or any website, or any combination thereof, including any injury or damage to Your or any other person's computer related to or resulting from participation or downloading any materials in the Competition. If for any reason a contestant’s entry cannot be viewed or is not capable of running as planned, including infection by computer viruses, bugs, tampering, unauthorized intervention, fraud or technical failures, the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility.

10. In no event will the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates, subsidiaries and related companies, Event Partners, its advertising or promotion agencies, or its officers, directors, employees, shareholders, representatives or agents be responsible or liable for any damages or losses of any kind, including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages arising out of any Entrant’s access to and use of the Website. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, everything on the Website is provided "as is"without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied, including but not limited to, the implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for purpose or use or non-infringement.

11. You agree to participate in related publicity and to the use of Your name and likeness for the purposes of advertising, promotion and publicity without additional compensation.

12. If shortlisted entrants are unable to supply a high resolution image of at least 5MB and 300ppi their entry may be disqualified.

13. There are no cash alternatives available for prize winners.

13.1 Prize winners may receive digital imaging equipment as part of their prize and in such cases equipment may be sent to them. In some countries income tax may be applicable to prizes. It is the winner’s responsibility to pay any income taxes related to the prize in compliance with their own country’s law. In such cases the Winner agrees to indemnify and keep the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates or partners indemnified against any tax liability, charges, fines, penalties or interest or any other liability incurred by the winner which liability arose as a result of prizes provided to the Winner.

13.1.i Valid ETAs or Standard Visas to the UK are needed to attend the ceremony. It is the responsibility of the Entrant to acquire their own visa or entry forms. The Promoter is not responsible for the cost of the Entrant’s visa application and entry forms.

13.2 The Photographer of the Year prize offers the winner a solo presentation at the Sony World Photography Awards exhibition at Somerset House the following year. The exhibited images must comply with the World Photography Organisation’s rules. The winner will work closely with the World Photography Organisation and the exhibition curator on the allocated space, presentation and curation of the exhibition. Final decisions on space, production and cost remains with the World Photography Organisation. Any associated travel and accommodation costs will not be covered by the World Photography Organisation.

14. Winners will be announced online and at a black-tie ceremony in London.

Promoter: World Photography Organisation, Creo Arts Group Limited, 9 Manchester Square, London, United Kingdom.

Single Image competition (Previously Open competition)

The Single Image competition celebrates the power of a standalone photograph. Enter your best single images - you could win $5,000, a range of top Sony Digital Imaging equipment plus benefit from international media exposure.

Free to enter and open to anyone submitting single images taken in 2026

Enter up to three single images for free

Ten diverse categories to enter

Awards category winners plus up to 15 shortlisted photographers per category

One overall winner receives the Single Image Competition Winner title

Please see 'Rules' below for full image eligibility criteria

Deadline is 5 January, 2027 at 16.00 GMT

Want to enter more than three images? Buy image bundles and submit as many photographs as you like. More information is available in your account.

PRIZES

Overall Winner

Category Winner

Shortlist

Win $5,000 (USD)

**Might be digital depending on position

Rules

The Single Image competition celebrates the power of a standalone photograph across ten (10) categories. Photographers should consider the category description when entering their work. Judges are looking for good composition, creativity and clear photographs.

If you enter the Single Image competition, you can also enter the Series competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

1.1 By entering the Competition You hereby accept these Competition Rules and the Terms and Conditions.

1.2.1 The Competition is free to enter.

1.2.2 The Single Image competition is open to all members of the public.

1.3 Entries must be submitted by 5 January, 2027 - 16.00 GMT.

1.4 By entering the Competition, You agree and acknowledge that the World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive Your registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation in accordance with its Privacy Policy.

1.5 If you enter the Single Image competition, you can also enter the Series competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

2. To enter, you must upload your image via the World Photography Organisation Website ( www.worldphoto.org ) or any of the official Sony World Photography Awards’ websites and follow the on-screen instructions carefully.

2.1 Images must be taken in 2026 and entries should be based on the Categories outlined, information on which can be found on the Website. Entrants can submit a photograph that has been taken, entered in another competition, won an award, or been published in books, magazines, newspapers, online and printed editorials, self-published websites, and gallery exhibitions between 1 January 2026 and 5 January 2027.

2.2 Images should be no smaller than 1MB and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files. All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model.

3.1 Entries will be judged between January 6 and January 31, 2027.

3.2 A shortlist of up to fifteen (15) photographers from each category and category winners will be selected and announced prior to April 2027; the overall winner will be announced in April 2027.

3.3 The individual category winners and the Single Image competition winner of the Sony World Photography Awards, will be voted for by the Judges and notified by email.

3.4 The decision of the Judges and the World Photography Organisation is final and no negotiation will be entered into with respect to any such decision.

3.5 Each Entrant can submit up to three images for free. The images entered can be entered in different categories or all images can be entered into a single category. Judging will be based on the single image and not the series of images.

3.5.2. During the judging process successful entries may be moved to a different category to the category they originally entered into. The decision will be made at the discretion of the judging panel. Successful entrants will be notified of the change over email.

4. Your Entry may feature manipulation, but where Entries are manipulated, the extent of which must be described in the image description section when submitting. For the avoidance of doubt, all Entries must originally be from either an analogue or digital photograph which may have then been manipulated. Computer generated content cannot be the origin of the Entry. Should a question arise through the judging process regarding the extent of your Entry’s manipulation you may be requested to submit the original photograph and image file to verify.

4.1 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to disqualify and remove any entry that does not comply with the following requirements, even after the entry is submitted on the Website. You warrant and represent, in respect of each entry submitted by You (“Entry”), as follows:

4.1.1 You are the sole owner and author of each Entry

4.1.2 You have the right to make Your Entry available to the Competition

4.1.3 Each Entry does not contain personally identifiable information about You or any other person(s)

4.1.4 Each Entry does not contain any infringing, threatening, false, misleading, abusive, harassing, libellous-, defamatory, vulgar, obscene, scandalous, inflammatory, pornographic or profane content

4.1.5 Each Entry does not contain any material that could constitute or encourage conduct which would be considered a criminal offence, give rise to civil liability, or otherwise violate any law

4.1.6 Each Entry does not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, contract rights, or any other intellectual property rights of any third person or entity, or violate any person’s rights of privacy or publicity, including:

4.1.6.1 trademarks owned by third parties

4.1.6.2 copyrighted materials owned by third parties (including movie dialogue or musical compositions)

4.1.6.3 names, likenesses, voices or other characteristics identifying celebrities or other public figures, living or dead

4.1.7 Entries which contain any commercial content that promotes any product or service other than that of the World Photography Organisation .

4.1.8 Entries containing screen credits

4.1.9 No animals were harmed, manipulated or distressed in the making of the image.

This includes, but is not limited to:

Deliberately disturbing or provoking an animal to capture a reaction

Using tape lures or decoys to attract animals or trigger a behaviour

Live baiting of any kind

Using flash photography on nocturnal birds

Failing to adhere to applicable laws, rules and permissions when working with wildlife and in natural environments, for example with protected species or protected environments

4.1.10 Archival images may be used when creating new work where any usage maintains compliance with clause 2. All archival images must be used with the required permissions. Usage of archival images must be stated in the description.

4.1.11 Drone usage must comply with the laws, rules, and permissions of the country in which the image was taken. The Promoter may request proof of permissions where applicable.

4.2 You agree to fully indemnify the World Photography Organisation in respect of all royalties, fees and any other monies owing to any person by reason of Your breaching any of the foregoing.

4.3 You confirm that each person depicted in the Entry has granted permission to be portrayed as shown. Any costumes, props or other materials used must be rented or borrowed with the permission of the owner, and all other relevant permissions must have been obtained.

4.4 In accordance with clause 3.2 and 3.3 all shortlisted and winning photographers will be contacted by email. If the World Photography Organisation does not hear from the entrant by the date specified in any correspondence and is therefore not able to ratify the entry that entrant will be disqualified and replaced by another photographer.

5.1 If you are under 16, you have Your parent’s or legal guardian’s consent to participate in the Competition.

5.2 If the World Photography Organisation does not receive a valid signed parental or legal guardian consent form for any winner under the age of 16 within 7 clear days of the Entrant being declared a winner (excluding the day on which such declaration is made by the World Photography Organisation ) the World Photography Organisation will be entitled to select an alternative winner from among the Entrants.

6. The World Photography Organisation may run an online rating process whereby members of the public may vote for a favourite photograph. If there is sufficient evidence (in the World Photography Organisation’s sole discretion) to suggest malpractice and manipulation of the rating process, then the World Photography Organisation has the right to remove the relevant Entry or Entries and, if necessary, award the prize to a different Entrant. the World Photography Organisation’s decisions are final.

7.1 The World Photography Organisation recognises You, the author of the image, retain full ownership of the copyright in each Entry.

7.2 All Entrants understand that any image submitted to the competition may be used by the World Photography Organisation, and its Event Partners, for marketing and promotional purposes of You the author and the event only, for a maximum of three years after the announcement in April 2027. You hereby grant the World Photography Organisation a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence in each Entry throughout the world for three years in all media for any use connected to the promotion of You the author and the Sony World Photography Awards event and/or competition, including, but not limited too:

(a) judging the Competition

(b) displaying the winning entries and runners up at public exhibitions promoting the World Photography Organisation and organised by the World Photography Organisation

(c) inclusion within the Website, a World Photography Awards book, magazine or similar

(d) inclusion within any materials promoting of the Competition and / or any exhibition organised by the World Photography Organisation , in the promotion of the World Photography Organisation

(e) inclusion on Competition- and exhibition-related products to be sold by the World Photography Organisation or any third party following the individual agreement by the author

(f) sub-licensing the Entries to the press for reproduction in connection with the Competition and any exhibition

(g) allowing viewers of the Website and/or Sony World Photography Awards Application to view images on a computer screen, PDA or mobile telephone and store such pages in electronic form on disk or on a PDA or mobile telephone (but not on any server or other storage device connected to a network) for their personal, non-commercial use only. Please also refer to clause 9.

(h) incorporation by the World Photography Organisation and Sony World Photography Awards Event Partners in Sony World Photography Awards Galleries and or Sony World Photography Awards Gallery Applications on Event Partner devices for a period of three (3) years after the applicable announcement date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, You hereby acknowledge and agree if Your image is included in such Sony World Photography Awards Galleries or Sony World Photography Awards Gallery Applications Your image will remain perpetually in the device royalty free.

7.3 All Entrants understand that the image information, including image name and description, may be shared with Event partners and media as per clause 7.1, 7.2 and 8. For the avoidance of doubt the “image information” does not include any personal information of You the author.

7.3.1 Should entrants elect to opt-in to sharing data, the email data and name will be shared with our event partners.

7.4 All entrants are required to enter under their correct names, and all entrants are responsible for providing this information accurately. The Awards programme is structured around providing opportunities and exposure to individual photographers and as such we do not award anonymously or accept pseudonyms.

7.5 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right to select which images be featured within the curated exhibit and such curation is made in its sole discretion. Associated image captions and bios may also be edited to fit within the context of the exhibition, book or other material connected to the Awards.

7.6 For Entrants that qualify for the National & Regional Award programme, the Promoter reserves the right not to award a winner if, in the opinion of the judges, none of the Entrants meet the required standard.

8. Any photograph used by the World Photography Organisation shall carry a credit line. Any failure to provide such credit line shall not be deemed to be a breach, as long as the World Photography Organisation uses its reasonable endeavours to rectify such failure within a reasonable period from the date of notice of such failure.

8a. All entrants understand the World Photography Organisation may need to crop your image or add text or logos when used specifically to promote your work or the Awards for online promotional purposes only.

9. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete information, whether caused by website users or by any of the equipment or programming associated with or utilised in the Competition, and the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for technical, hardware or software failures of any kind, for lost network connections, garbled computer transmissions, other problems or technical malfunctions with regard to the Competition. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any error, omission, corruption, interruption, deletion, defect, delay in operation or transmission, communications line failure, theft or destruction or unauthorized access to or alteration of Entries. the World Photography Organisation is not responsible for any problems or technical malfunction of any telephone network or lines, computer on-line systems, servers, computer equipment, software, failure of any e-mail addressed to the World Photography Organisation on account of technical problems, human error or traffic congestion on the internet or any website, or any combination thereof, including any injury or damage to Your or any other person's computer related to or resulting from participation or downloading any materials in the Competition. If for any reason a contestant’s entry cannot be viewed or is not capable of running as planned, including infection by computer viruses, bugs, tampering, unauthorized intervention, fraud or technical failures, the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility.

10. In no event will the World Photography Organisation , its parents, affiliates, subsidiaries and related companies, Event Partners, its advertising or promotion agencies, or its officers, directors, employees, shareholders, representatives or agents be responsible or liable for any damages or losses of any kind, including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages arising out of any Entrant’s access to and use of the Website. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, everything on the Website is provided "as is"without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied, including but not limited to, the implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for purpose or use or non-infringement.

11. You agree to participate in related publicity and to the use of Your name and likeness for the purposes of advertising, promotion and publicity without additional compensation.

12. If shortlisted entrants are unable to supply a high resolution image of at least 5MB and 300ppi their entry may be disqualified.

13. There are no cash alternatives available for prize winners.

13.1 Prize winners may receive digital imaging equipment as part of their prize and in such cases equipment may be sent to them. In some countries income tax may be applicable to prizes. It is the winner’s responsibility to pay any income taxes related to the prize in compliance with their own country’s law. In such cases the Winner agrees to indemnify and keep the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates or partners indemnified against any tax liability, charges, fines, penalties or interest or any other liability incurred by the winner which liability arose as a result of prizes provided to the Winner.

13.1.i Valid ETAs or Standard Visas to the UK are needed to attend the ceremony. It is the responsibility of the Entrant to acquire their own visa or entry forms. The Promoter is not responsible for the cost of the Entrant’s visa application and entry forms.

14. Winner will be announced online and at a black-tie ceremony in London.

Promoter: World Photography Organisation, Creo Arts Group Limited, 9 Manchester Square, London, United Kingdom.

Student competition

Providing a platform for photography students worldwide. Prizes include top Sony Digital Imaging equipment, inclusion in the London exhibition and the annual book - plus more!

Free to enter for anyone aged from 18 to 30 years-old undertaking a photography programme*

Students answer a set brief with 5 to 10 images

Up to 10 shortlisted photographers

One overall winner receives the Student Competition Winner title

Deadline for entries is 27 November 2026 at 16:00 (GMT)

2027 Student brief: Journeys

Journeys are a universal theme across cultures and languages, and can take many shapes. They have been explored in countless works of art, fiction and non-fiction, and in photography. For this year’s brief, we invite students to explore the theme of Journeys from their own perspective.

Considering the idea of Journeys in its broadest sense, we encourage you to interpret this theme in a way that feels meaningful to you. From the rites of passage that shape a child’s coming of age, to the transformations that shape our cities, to the small, day-to-day changes within a particular community, to migrations of animals across continents, life across the globe is marked by movement and change. We invite you to depict a journey of your choice, through a photographic series of five to 10 images.

Your images can be taken on any device, shot in any style, and approached from any angle you feel is best. While creative responses are encouraged, photographers must stick to the brief.

If your institution is not registered yet, you can register here . For a list of participating institutions, please see here .

*A programme refers to a formalised photography course/credit/module/foundation which is taught at higher education level, within a diploma / Bachelor of Arts / Master of Arts curriculum.

Rules

The Student competition provides a platform for photography students and universities worldwide. Students must submit series of minimum five (5) and a maximum of ten (10) images, responding to the annual brief.

1. The Competition is open to all students of photography from World Photography Organisation’s selected Universities. All Entrants must be aged between 18 and 30 years of age at the time of Competition’s deadline. All entries must confirm, on application, their acceptance of the rules of the Competition and these Terms and Conditions. Entries must be submitted by 16.00 GMT on 27 November 2026. By entering the Competition, each Entrant agrees and acknowledges that World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive his/her registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation in accordance with its privacy policy.

2. Students are required to submit Five (5) - Ten (10) images responding to a brief. To enter, students must ensure their institution is registered and images are submitted via www.worldphoto.org .

2.1 Images must be taken in the 18 months prior to the competition closing date of 27 November 2026. Entries should be based on the Brief outlined, information on which can be found on the Website. 2.2 Published work may have been taken in the 18 months prior to the competition closing date of 27 November 2026, but must have been first published between the dates of 1 January 2026 and 27 November 2026.

Up to 20% of work can be published at any point in time on your personal website, social media or exhibited as part of an official programme i.e. two images can be published on personal platforms at any point in time if submitting a series of 8-10 images. One image can be published at any point in time if submitting a series of 5-7 images. 2.3 Images should be no smaller than 1MB and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files. All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model and EXIF data must be left in the image file. 2.4 All Entrants, if they are selected amongst the shortlist, must be able to supply a high resolution image suitable for printing in exhibitions should the image be required. 3.1 All entries to be uploaded by 13.00 GMT on 27 November 2026.

3.2 Images from all participating students will then be judged by the selected World Photography Organisation judging panel to choose a shortlist and overall winner. The selected shortlist will be announced after being deemed suitable by the World Photography Organisation after January 1, 2027.

3.3 The overall winner will be announced in April 2027.

You hereby grant the World Photography Organisation a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence in each Entry throughout the world for three years in all media for any use connected to the promotion of You the author and the Sony World Photography Awards Event and/or Competition, including, but not limited too: (a) judging the Competition (b) displaying the winning and shortlisted entries at public exhibitions promoting the World Photography Organisation and organised by the World Photography Organisation (c) inclusion within the Website, a World Photography Awards book, magazine or similar (d) inclusion within any materials promoting of the Competition and / or any exhibition organised by the World Photography Organisation, in the promotion of the World Photography Organisation (e) inclusion on Competition- and exhibition-related products to be sold by the World Photography Organisation or any third party following the individual agreement by the author (f) sub-licensing the Entries to the press for reproduction in connection with the Competition and any exhibition (g) allowing viewers of the Website to view images on a computer screen, PDA or mobile telephone and store such pages in electronic form on disk or on a PDA or mobile telephone (but not on any server or other storage device connected to a network) for their personal, non-commercial use only. content.article_text:
Youth competition

Open to photographers aged 19 and under. Entry is free and you could win top Sony Digital Imaging equipment, inclusion in the London exhibition and the annual book - plus more!

Competition runs from 1 June 2026 to 5 January 2027

Photographers can enter up to three images relating to a theme

Judges will select a shortlist of up to 10 photographers

Shortlist compete for Youth Competition Winner title

Overall winner receives Youth Competition Winner title and Sony Digital Imaging kit

Please see 'Rules' below for full image eligibility criteria

Deadline for entries is 5 January 2027 at 16:00 (GMT)

PRIZES

Overall winner

Shortlist - up to 9

Receive Sony Digital Imaging equipment

x

Flights and accommodation to the awards ceremony in London

x

Certificate **

x

Trophy

x

Global press exposure

x

x

Copy of the book

x

Inclusion in book

x

Inclusion in exhibition*

x

Promoted on our website

x

x

Promoted to our online community

x

x

*Please note, your image may be displayed digitally (on screens) or printed

**Might be digital depending on position

Rules

The Youth competition celebrates standout single images shot by photographers aged 19 and under.

1.1 By entering the Competition You hereby accept these Competition Rules and the Terms and Conditions.

1.2 .1 The competition is free to enter.

1.2.2 The Youth competition is open to all members of the public aged 19 and under on the closing date of the competition.

1.3 Entries must be submitted between June 1, 2026 and 5 January 2027 at 16:00 (GMT).

1.4 By entering the Competition, You agree and acknowledge that the World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive your registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation in accordance with its Privacy Policy.

2. To enter, you must upload your image via the World Photography Organisation Website ( www.worldphoto.org ) or any of the official Sony World Photography Award websites and follow the on-screen instructions carefully.

2.1 Images must be taken in 2026 and Entries should be based on the theme outlined, information on which can be found on the Website. Entrants can submit a photograph that has been taken, entered in another competition, won an award, or been published in books, magazines, newspapers, online and printed editorials, self-published websites, and gallery exhibitions between 1 January 2026 and 5 January 2027.

2.2 Images should be no smaller than 1mb and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files. All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model.

2.2.1 If entrants are unable to supply a high resolution image of at least 5MB and 300ppi their entry may be disqualified.

3.1 The overall winner will be selected between 5 January 2027 and March 2027

3.2 The winner and a shortlist will be selected and announced prior to April 2027 and the overall winner will be announced in April 2027.

3.3 The Youth Competition winner will be voted for by the Judges. The overall winner of the Youth Competition, will be notified by email.

3.4 The decision of the Judges and the World Photography Organisation is final and no negotiation will be entered into with respect to any such decision.

3.5 Each Entrant can submit up to three (3) images for free. Judging will be based on the single image and not a series of images.

4. Your Entry may feature manipulation, but where Entries are manipulated, the extent of which must be described in the image description section when submitting. For the avoidance of doubt, all Entries must originally be from either an analogue or digital photograph which may have then been manipulated. Computer generated content cannot be the origin of the Entry. Should a question arise through the judging process regarding the extent of your Entry’s manipulation you may be requested to submit the original photograph and image file to verify.

4.1 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to disqualify and remove any entry that does not comply with the following requirements, even after the entry is submitted on the Website. You warrant and represent, in respect of each entry submitted by You (“Entry”), as follows:

4.1.1 You are the sole owner and author of each Entry

4.1.2 You have the right to make Your entry available to the Competition

4.1.3 Each Entry does not contain personally identifiable information about You or any other person(s)

4.1.4 Each Entry does not contain any infringing, threatening, false, misleading, abusive, harassing, libellous, defamatory, vulgar, obscene, scandalous, inflammatory, pornographic or profane content

4.1.5 Each Entry does not contain any material that could constitute or encourage conduct which would be considered a criminal offence, give rise to civil liability, or otherwise violate any law

4.1.6 Each Entry does not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, contract rights, or any other intellectual property rights of any third person or entity, or violate any person’s rights of privacy or publicity, and Your Entry does not include:

4.1.6.1 Trademarks owned by third parties

4.1.6.2 Copyrighted materials owned by third parties (including movie dialogue or musical compositions)

4.1.6.3 Names, likenesses, voices or other characteristics identifying celebrities or other public figures, living or dead

4.1.7 Entries which contain any commercial content that promotes any product or service other than that of the World Photography Organisation.

4.1.8 Entries containing screen credits

4.1.9 No animals were harmed, manipulated or distressed in the making of the image. This includes, but is not limited to:

Deliberately disturbing or provoking an animal to capture a reaction

Using tape lures or decoys to attract animals or trigger a behaviour

Live baiting of any kind

Using flash photography on nocturnal birds

Failing to adhere to applicable laws, rules and permissions when working with wildlife and in natural environments, for example with protected species or protected environments

4.1.10 Archival images may be used when creating new work where any usage maintains compliance with clause 2. All archival images must be used with the required permissions. Usage of archival images must be stated in the description.

4.1.11 Drone usage must comply with the laws, rules, and permissions of the country in which the image was taken. The Promoter may request proof of permissions where applicable.

4.2 You agree to fully indemnify the World Photography Organisation in respect of all royalties, fees and any other monies owing to any person by reason of Your breaching any of the foregoing.

4.3 You confirm that each person depicted in the Entry has granted permission to be portrayed as shown. Any costumes, props or other materials used must be rented or borrowed with the permission of the owner, and all other relevant permissions must have been obtained.

4.4 In accordance with clause 3.2 and 3.3 all shortlisted and winning photographers will be contacted by email. If the World Photography Organisation does not hear from the entrant by the date specified in any correspondence and is therefore not able to ratify the entry that entrant will be disqualified and replaced by another photographer.

5.1 If you are under 16, you have Your parent’s or legal guardian’s consent to participate in the Competition.

5.2 If the World Photography Organisation does not receive a valid signed parental or legal guardian consent form for any winner under the age of 16 within 7 clear days of the Entrant being declared a winner (excluding the day on which such declaration is made by the World Photography Organisation) the World Photography Organisation will be entitled to select an alternative winner from among the Entrants.

6. The World Photography Organisation may run an online rating process whereby members of the public may vote for a favourite photograph. content.article_text:
1. Introduction

Greetings.

Welcome to the Do Ho Suh exhibition at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea.

With works found in cities around the world, including Seoul, New York, and London, Do Ho Suh is well established as a leading South Korean installation artist.

This large-scale solo exhibition explores Suh’s artistic practice, shaped by his distinctive visual language over the past three decades.

For this artist who grew up in Seoul but has mainly worked abroad, personal movement has been a process through which different cultures, languages, systems, and communities have intersected, collided, and overlapped. For Suh, a home is not merely a fixed building set in a specific place. It is a sensory space that moves with the body, carries memories around the world, and connects a person’s experiences with those of others. His conception of home is not something unique to those who cross borders, like Suh. Every day that we open our doors and step outside, we, too, become nomads as we leave the familiar behind and adapt to a different world. Suh’s work has a universal resonance, and he is internationally recognized among the prominent artists of our time.

This exhibition includes previously unseen early works and drawings. They offer a glimpse into the questions he explored and the experiments he performed at the beginning of his career, while also demonstrating his playful imagination. The exhibition presents a broad selection of Suh’s works, including some of his most recent pieces, as it traces how his ideas have shifted and expanded over the last thirty years. It is hoped that it will prove to be another milestone along Suh’s journey as an artist who continues to evolve and create. It is also hoped that it will become a space where our questions intersect and intertwine with each other’s and, ideally, a home where the memories and questions of each of us can linger.

The works in this exhibition are not organized according to theme. Instead, the exhibition arranges the early and later works, drawings, and installations to reflect on and expand upon the concepts of home and the body and of space and time within a cohesive context. As you move through the web of relationships Suh has woven among these concepts, you can take a moment to add your own memories and experiences to what you encounter.

content.article_text:
The wind whooshes. The leaves rustle. Footsteps go pitter-patter.

Artist Kim Joon, children from Seoul Metropolitan Children’s Hospital, and their families explored the museum and its surroundings. Together, they listened to the world around them, recorded what they heard, and turned those sounds into works of art.

The exhibition Crinkle, Crinkle, Whisper, Whisper grew out of their seven-week journey through sound and the senses.

Take a moment to listen closely.

The world has more stories to tell than you might think.

content.article_text:
Here in the Seoul Box, we are standing in a symbolic space of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea. This space currently hosts the second exhibition of the MMCA×LG OLED Series, which launched for the first time last year. This collaborative project was developed by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea in partnership with LG Electronics. By combining advanced display technology and artistic imagination, this series offers visitors new ways of experiencing contemporary art.

For this year's edition, artist Christine Sun Kim has transformed this space by utilizing the architectural characteristics of the Seoul Box to create a monumental installation consisting of large-scale digital animation and wall drawings. Artist Christine Sun Kim, a Berlin-based Korean American, has explored language, sound, and structures of communication across a diverse range of media, including drawing, moving image, and performance. She has gained significant recognition in the contemporary art world, including being ranked 34th on a 2025 British contemporary art magazine list of the most influential figures in international contemporary art.

Kim has developed a distinctive artistic language that translates communicative language into visual form. Rooted in the experiences of deaf communities, her work draws upon a wide range of visual elements, including American Sign Language, musical notation, the motion lines of comic books, handwritten drawings, diagrams, and text. Through these elements, Kim visually reveals how language forms and transforms interpersonal relationships, and how it connects us to the world at large.

Her work invites us to reconsider the systems and conventions of communication that we often take for granted. In recent years, her practice has expanded beyond individual drawings and performances into immersive spatial environments, transforming language itself into a three-dimensional experience. Within this space, we are invited to experience the ways in which language is generated, moves, and collides through multiple senses.

Welcome to «Korea Artist Prize 2026» exhibition. Co-organized by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea and the SBS Foundation, the Korea Artist Prize is one of the most prestigious art awards and artist support programs in Korea. This year’s artists are Lee Hai Min Sun, Lee Jungwoo, Jeon Hyunsun, and Hong Jin-hwon. Peau d’Homme

Un film de Léa Domenach

Avec Claire Pommet, Catherine Deneuve, Karin Viard, Louis Peres, Stefan Crépon

Genre :

Durée : 1h44

Note : Si le téléchargement ne fonctionne pas en cliquant directement sur un lien, veuillez cliquer avec le bouton droit sur ce lien et choisir l'option "Enregistrer la cible du lien sous..." ou "Enregistrer le lien sous..." ou "Télécharger le fichier lié sous..." suivant votre navigateur.

En 1480 et des poussières, alors que la princesse Blanche se prépare à épouser le beau prince du royaume voisin, son père décide de la marier à Melchior, son vulgaire chef des armées. C’est alors que sa marraine lui révèle être en possession d’une mystérieuse "peau" qui va permettre à Blanche, si elle la revêt, de devenir un homme, et ainsi de faire connaissance avec son fiancé incognito.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Cult

Rogue Trooper

Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Duncan Jones

With Aneurin Barnard, Matt Berry, Hayley Atwell

UK 2026. 120min

Courtesy of Liberty Films Rebellion

Language English

Access information

Monday 12 October 20:35

Descriptive subtitles

Friday 16 October 12:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Biochipped genetic soldiers, whose personalities can be downloaded should they fall on the battlefield, fight a futile, violent war across a chemically toxic landscape. Time is of the essence for their mission, but a raft of horrors await them. Fast and funny, Rogue Trooper is skilfully directed by Jones (Moon and Source Code), who gives this terrific British indie the feel of a Hollywood blockbuster.

Justin Johnson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

Bassam Tariq follows Mogul Mowgli (LFF 2020) with this gripping, inventive thriller, featuring a commanding central performance by Oscar winner Mahershala Ali.

Klara and the Sun

Oscar winner Taika Waititi’s luminous adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s bestselling novel sees Jenna Ortega play an enthusiastic artificial friend desperate to find a loving home.
